definition_zh: 疏远；疏离感；（哲学）异化；（法律）转让
definition_en: the state of feeling isolated from people, work or society; in social theory, estrangement from your own labour; in law, the transfer of property
core_image: 站在人群里却觉得隔着一层玻璃
scene: 搬进新城市半年，他每天上班打卡，却谁也不认识。Alienation grew quietly behind his polite smile.
sceneCN: 这里 alienation 是「疏离感」（第 1 个义项：与周围人或环境失去联系的心理状态）；句意为疏离感在他礼貌的微笑背后悄悄滋长。核心画面是站在人群里却觉得隔着一层玻璃。

forms.label: 不可数名词，无复数形式

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ion 的动词，义为「使疏远；转让」
过去分词作形容词，义为「感到被疏远的」
同根形容词，义为「外国的；陌生的」

senses.title: The feeling of being cut off
senses.definition: the state of feeling isolated from the people, work or society around you, as though a wall stood between you and them
senses.definitionCN: 感到与周围的人、工作或社会隔绝的状态，仿佛彼此之间立着一道墙
senses.example: Long shifts and empty weekends deepened his alienation.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的班次与空荡的周末加深了他的疏离感。
senses.why: Alien means other, and -ation names a state, so alienation is the state of having become other: you are among people yet no longer of them.
senses.whyCN: alien 意为「他者」，-ation 表示状态，所以 alienation 就是「已成为他者」的状态：你在人群之中，却不再属于他们。

senses.title: Loss of control over your own work
senses.definition: in social theory, the condition in which workers lose control over what they make and feel estranged from their own labour
senses.definitionCN: 社会理论中，劳动者失去对自己产品的控制、并与自身劳动相疏离的状态
senses.example: Marx described alienation as the worker lost in the product.
senses.exampleCN: 马克思把异化描述为劳动者在自己的产品中失落。
senses.why: This sense narrows the general wall to one specific place: the workshop, where what you build no longer feels like yours.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把那堵普遍的墙收窄到一个具体场所：车间，你造出来的东西不再感觉属于你。

senses.title: The legal transfer of property
senses.definition: in law, the act of transferring ownership of property to another person, the oldest sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 法律上把财产所有权转移给他人的行为，是该词最古老的用法
senses.example: The deed records the alienation of the family farm.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据记录了家族农场的转让。
senses.why: Here the word stays literal: making a thing alien means making it the property of someone else, which is precisely what a transfer does.
senses.whyCN: 这里该词保持字面义：让某物变成 alien「别人的」，正是转让所做的事。

intro.en: Alienation is the noun of alienate: Latin alienus, belonging to another, plus the process suffix -ation, naming the state of having been made other.
intro.cn: alienation 是 alienate 的名词形式：拉丁语 alienus「属于别人的」加过程后缀 -ation，表示「已被变成他者」的状态。

items.en: Latin alius meant other, the root of alias, alibi and alter.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alius 意为「其他」，是 alias、alibi 与 alter 的词根。

items.en: Alienus meant belonging to another, and so foreign, strange or unrelated.
items.cn: alienus 意为「属于别人的」，因此引申为外国的、陌生的、无关的。

items.en: The noun alienatio named a transfer of ownership in Roman law, and also a loss of reason or affection.
items.cn: 名词 alienatio 在罗马法中指所有权转让，也指理智或感情的丧失。

items.en: Old French alienation kept the legal sense, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 alienation 保留法律义，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: Philosophy and sociology widened the word in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries to name estrangement from work and society.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，哲学与社会学拓宽该词，用以指与劳动和社会的疏离。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the ali- family of otherness; the near-meaning group lists other words for feeling cut off.
note.cn: 形近组保留表示「他者」的 ali- 词族；近义组列出其他表示「感到隔绝」的词。

entries.definition: To make someone cold or hostile.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人变得冷淡或敌对。

entries.definition: Belonging to another place or person.
entries.definitionCN: 属于别处或别人的。

entries.definition: Feeling isolated and unwanted.
entries.definitionCN: 感到孤立、不被接纳的。

entries.definition: A change made to something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物所做的改动。

entries.definition: The state of being alone and separated.
entries.definitionCN: 独自一人与外界分离的状态。

entries.definition: The loss of affection between people.
entries.definitionCN: 人与人之间感情的丧失。

entries.definition: Sadness at being alone.
entries.definitionCN: 因独处而产生的难过。

entries.definition: A break in a link or relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 联系或关系的中断。

normalIntro.en: Alienation is alienate plus -ion: the state produced when someone is made alien.
normalIntro.cn: alienation 就是 alienate 加 -ion：把某人变成外人之后产生的那种状态。

normal.en: Alienate is the verb, alienation the result: one pushes, the other is the distance left.
normal.cn: alienate 是动词，alienation 是结果：一个是推，一个是推完后留下的距离。

normal.en: Alien means other, so alienation is otherness turned into a feeling.
normal.cn: alien 意为「他者」，所以 alienation 就是「他者性」变成的一种感受。

normal.en: It is uncountable, so say a sense of alienation, not an alienation.
normal.cn: 它不可数，所以说 a sense of alienation，不说 an alienation。

normal.en: In sociology alienation from work is a fixed phrase; keep the from.
normal.cn: 社会学中 alienation from work 是固定搭配，别丢掉 from。

normal.en: In law the alienation of property simply means its transfer.
normal.cn: 法律上 the alienation of property 就是财产转让。

abstract.en: Picture standing in a crowded room behind a sheet of glass.
abstract.cn: 想象站在拥挤的房间里，面前隔着一层玻璃。

abstract.en: Imagine building a chair all day and never being allowed to sit in it.
abstract.cn: 想象整天做椅子，却从不被允许坐上去。

abstract.en: Think of your own name written on a door you can no longer open.
abstract.cn: 想象你自己的名字写在一扇你再也打不开的门上。

examples.en: Alienation often follows a long move to a new city.
examples.cn: 搬到一个新城市后，疏离感常常随之而来。

examples.en: The survey measured alienation among night-shift workers.
examples.cn: 这项调查测量了夜班工人的疏离感。

examples.en: Any alienation of the land needs the consent of both heirs.
examples.cn: 这块土地的任何转让都需两位继承人同意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诶里诶内申」——诶里（alien）是外人，诶内申（ation）是状态：变成外人的那种状态，就是疏离、异化。

root: 拉丁语 alius「其他」派生出 alienus「属于别人的」，加动词后缀构成 alienare「转让、使疏远」，其名词 alienatio 经古法语 alienation 进入英语，字面即「被变成他者的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses describe the same crossing: a person becomes other to their community, a worker becomes other to their product, and a property becomes other to its owner.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项描述的是同一次跨越：人对自己的社群成为他者，劳动者对自己的产品成为他者，财产对原主成为他者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass wall between you and what was yours
core.cn: 核心意象：你与原本属于你的一切之间隔着一层玻璃

branches.en: A polite smile hiding no real contact.
branches.cn: 礼貌的微笑背后没有真正的接触。

branches.en: A new city where nobody knows your name.
branches.cn: 一座没人知道你名字的新城市。

branches.en: A worker who never owns what they build.
branches.cn: 从不拥有自己产品的劳动者。

branches.en: A deed moving land to another name.
branches.cn: 把土地转到别人名下的契据。

branches.en: All three make what was yours into the property of another.
branches.cn: 三者都把原本属于你的变成别人的。

intro.en: Alienation keeps the ali- root of otherness, the verb suffix -ate and the result suffix -ion, so the whole history is visible in the spelling.
intro.cn: alienation 保留表示「他者」的 ali- 词根、动词后缀 -ate 与结果后缀 -ion，整段历史都写在拼写里。

latinIntro.en: Latin alius gave alienus, alienare and the noun alienatio, which French passed to English with both senses intact.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alius 派生出 alienus、alienare 与名词 alienatio，法语把它传给英语时两义都完好保留。

latinEntries.example: Alius is the root of ali-.
latinEntries.exampleCN: alius 是 ali- 的词根。

definition_zh: （从马车、自行车上）下来；降落；燃烧着；点亮
definition_en: to step down or land after a journey, or burning and lit up
core_image: 鸟落枝头与火苗蹿起：同一个词的两个去向
scene: 火车进站停稳，她拎着行李下了车。The passengers alighted from the carriage one by one.
sceneCN: 这里 alight 是「下来、下车」（第 1 个义项：从车上走下）；句意是乘客们一个接一个从车厢下来。

derivatives.zh: alight 加 -ing 转作名词，义为「下车；着陆」
同根基础词，义为「光；轻」，alight 由两个不同来源的 light 各构成一义

senses.title: To step down from a vehicle
senses.definition: to step out of or off a train, bus, or horse, a formal word
senses.definitionCN: 从火车、公共汽车或马上下来，正式用语
senses.example: She alighted from the train into the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她下了火车，走进雨里。
senses.why: From the adjective 'light' in its old sense of getting off a horse: to go lightly to the ground.
senses.whyCN: 来自形容词 light 的古义「下马」：轻身落地。

senses.title: To land on something
senses.definition: to come down and settle on a place or object, as a bird or insect does
senses.definitionCN: 落下来停在某个地方或物体上，如鸟或昆虫
senses.example: A dragonfly alighted on the tip of the oar.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蜻蜓落在桨尖上。
senses.why: The same 'light landing' picture passes from riders to birds: whatever settles gently has alighted.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「轻落」画面从骑手转到鸟儿：凡轻轻停歇者皆可说 alight。

senses.title: Burning or glowing
senses.definition: on fire, or shining brightly with emotion or light
senses.definitionCN: 着火的；或因光亮、情绪而发亮
senses.example: The barn was set alight by a stray spark.
senses.exampleCN: 谷仓被一粒飞散的火星点燃。
senses.why: Here the base is the other light, fire and brightness: a- plus light gives 'in a state of flame or glow'.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词基是另一个 light（火光）：a- 加 light 表示「处于燃烧或发光的状态」。

intro.en: One form with two ancestors: a- plus light 'not heavy, dismount', and a- plus light 'fire, brightness'.
intro.cn: 一个词形，两个祖先：a- 加 light「不重的；下马」，以及 a- 加 light「火；光」。

items.en: *lingwh- is the reconstructed root behind light 'brightness'; *lingw- 'not heavy' shares the form by coincidence of sound.
items.cn: 重构词根 *lingwh- 是 light「光」的来源；表「不重」的 light 与之同形纯属音合。

items.en: leoht meant light and brightness; liht meant not heavy.
items.cn: 古英语 leoht 意为光、光亮；liht 意为不重的。

items.en: alighten meant to dismount, from the 'not heavy' light; alighten also meant to shine.
items.cn: 中古英语 alighten 既指下马（来自「轻」），也指发光（来自「光」）。

items.en: The verb narrowed to stepping down and landing; the adjective settled as 'burning, glowing'.
items.cn: 16 世纪动词义收窄为下车与降落；形容词义定型为「燃烧、发亮」。

items.en: The verb is now formal; the adjective survives in phrases like set alight.
items.cn: 现代英语中动词属正式用语；形容词存于 set alight 等短语。

note.en: The first group gathers both light roots and a sound-alike; the second gathers words for landing and burning.
note.cn: 第一组收两个 light 词源与音近词；第二组收「降落」与「燃烧」的近义词。

entries.definition: brightness, or not heavy; the double base of alight
entries.definitionCN: 光；轻——alight 的双重词基

entries.definition: the act of stepping down or landing
entries.definitionCN: 下车；降落

entries.definition: great pleasure; only looks similar, from Latin delectare
entries.definitionCN: 欣喜；仅形近，源自拉丁语 delectare

entries.definition: to get down from a horse or bicycle
entries.definitionCN: 下马；下车

entries.definition: to come down to the ground
entries.definitionCN: 着陆；落地

entries.definition: to settle on a raised place, as birds do
entries.definitionCN: （鸟）栖息；停在高处

entries.definition: burning fiercely, or brightly lit
entries.definitionCN: 燃烧的；光亮的

entries.definition: to set fire to, or to stir up a feeling
entries.definitionCN: 点燃；激起

normalIntro.en: a- plus light: a light landing, or a room full of light.
normalIntro.cn: a- 加 light：轻轻落下，或满屋亮光。

normal.en: alight from a bus is the formal way to say get off.
normal.cn: alight from a bus 是 get off 的正式说法。

normal.en: Birds alight on branches; the word pictures a light landing.
normal.cn: 鸟儿 alight on 枝头，词里画着一记轻落。

normal.en: set alight means to set fire to something.
normal.cn: set alight 意为点燃某物。

normal.en: Her eyes were alight with excitement: glowing.
normal.cn: 她的眼睛闪着兴奋的光：发亮。

normal.en: Two light words merged: light 'not heavy' and light 'brightness'.
normal.cn: 两个 light 合流：「轻」与「光」。

abstract.en: Picture a bird opening its wings just as its feet touch the branch.
abstract.cn: 想象鸟儿的脚刚触枝头便收拢翅膀。

abstract.en: See a lady stepping off a carriage skirt first, hand last.
abstract.cn: 想象一位女士下马车，裙摆先落，手随后。

abstract.en: Imagine a match flaring in a dark barn.
abstract.cn: 想象一根火柴在黑暗谷仓里划亮。

examples.en: Never alight from a moving bus.
examples.cn: 切勿从行驶中的公共汽车上下来。

examples.en: Snow alighted softly on the bare hedge.
examples.cn: 雪花轻轻落在光秃的树篱上。

examples.en: The old theatre was set alight by accident.
examples.cn: 老剧院被意外点燃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额来特」——轻得额前头发都不飘，落地一点声；火一点就亮。

root: alight 由中古英语 alighten 汇合两源：一为 a- 加 light「轻」（古英语 liht，指下马、轻落），一为 a- 加 light「光」（古英语 leoht，指燃烧、发亮）；两源同形不同根，今分别成动词与形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses from two roots: the 'light' root gives stepping down and birdlike landing, the 'light' root gives flame and glow.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项来自两个词根：「轻」根给出下车与鸟雀栖落，「光」根给出火焰与光亮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet touching the branch with barely a sound, or a match flaring in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚尖无声触枝，或火柴在黑暗中划亮。

branches.en: a skirted traveller stepping onto a station platform
branches.cn: 提裙走下站台的旅人

branches.en: a dragonfly resting on the tip of an oar
branches.cn: 停歇在桨尖的蜻蜓

branches.en: a thought landing on a listening mind
branches.cn: 落进倾听者心头的念头

branches.en: a barn lit from within by sudden fire
branches.cn: 被突燃的大火从内部照亮的谷仓

branches.en: two lights: one of weight, one of flame
branches.cn: 两个 light：一个是重量之轻，一个是火焰之光

intro.en: The prefix a- doing old English work on two different lights.
intro.cn: 前缀 a- 以古英语的方式作用在两个不同的 light 上。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root here; both lights are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 此处无拉丁词根；两个 light 均为日耳曼语源。

definition_zh: 对齐；排列成行；（立场、利益的）一致；结盟
definition_en: the arrangement of parts in a correct relative position or in a straight line; also the state of sharing the same goals, interests or loyalties
core_image: 把几样东西推到同一条直线上
scene: 四个轮子不在一条线上，方向盘总是往左偏。Wheel alignment fixed the pull in ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 alignment 是「对齐」（第 1 个义项：把部件调到同一条直线或正确相对位置）；句意为车轮定位十分钟就解决了跑偏。核心画面是把几样东西推到同一条直线上。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ment 的动词，义为「使对齐；使一致」
过去分词作形容词，义为「对齐的；立场一致的」
加 non- 构成，义为「不结盟」

senses.title: Arranging things in a straight line
senses.definition: the arrangement of parts in a correct relative position or in a straight line, used of wheels, text, bones and planets
senses.definitionCN: 把各部件调到正确的相对位置或排成一条直线，用于车轮、文本、骨骼与行星
senses.example: Check the alignment of the text before printing.
senses.exampleCN: 打印前检查文本的对齐方式。
senses.why: Align comes from a- plus line, so alignment is simply the state of being on one line: everything shares the same straight edge.
senses.whyCN: align 来自 a- 加 line，所以 alignment 就是「处在同一条线上」的状态：所有东西共享同一条直边。

senses.title: Agreement of aims or loyalties
senses.definition: the state of having the same goals, interests or loyalties as another person or group, used in politics and business
senses.definitionCN: 与他人或团体拥有相同目标、利益或忠诚的状态，用于政治与商业
senses.example: The merger requires alignment between the two boards.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并需要两个董事会达成一致。
senses.why: The same straight line is now drawn through intentions: when aims point the same way, people are said to be in alignment.
senses.whyCN: 同一条直线如今画在意图上：当目标指向同一方向，人们就被说成处于一致状态。

intro.en: Alignment is align plus -ment: the French ligne, a line, gave align, to put on a line, and English added the result suffix.
intro.cn: alignment 是 align 加 -ment：法语 ligne「线」产生 align「放到一条线上」，英语再加上表示结果的后缀。

items.en: Latin linea meant a linen thread and then a straight line, from linum, flax.
items.cn: 拉丁语 linea 先指亚麻线，后指直线，源自 linum「亚麻」。

items.en: Old French ligne kept the sense of line or row, and gave the verb lignier, to draw lines.
items.cn: 古法语 ligne 保留「线、行列」之义，并派生动词 lignier「画线」。

items.en: French aligner meant to put in a line, built from a-, to, plus ligne.
items.cn: 法语 aligner 意为「排成一行」，由 a-「向」加 ligne 构成。

items.en: English took align in the seventeenth century, first of troops drawn up in a row and of printed text.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 align，先用于列队的部队与排版的文本。

items.en: Adding -ment gave alignment, and the twentieth century extended it from mechanics to the agreement of policies and interests.
items.cn: 加 -ment 得到 alignment，二十世纪把它从机械领域引申到政策与利益的一致。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the line family; the near-meaning group lists other words for agreement or straight arrangement.
note.cn: 形近组保留 line 词族；近义组列出其他表示「一致」或「排成直线」的词。

entries.definition: To put in a line or bring into agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 排成一行或使一致。

entries.definition: Placed in line, or sharing the same aims.
entries.definitionCN: 排成直线的，或目标一致的。

entries.definition: A long thin mark or a row of things.
entries.definitionCN: 细长的标记或一排东西。

entries.definition: Arranged in or following a straight line.
entries.definitionCN: 排成直线的或沿直线的。

entries.definition: The state of sharing the same view.
entries.definitionCN: 持有相同看法的状态。

entries.definition: A pleasing fit between parts or people.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分或人与人之间协调的契合。

entries.definition: Organising parts so they work together.
entries.definitionCN: 组织各部分使其协同运作。

entries.definition: Behaviour matching a standard or group.
entries.definitionCN: 与标准或群体相符的行为。

normalIntro.en: Alignment is align plus -ment: the result of putting things on one line.
normalIntro.cn: alignment 就是 align 加 -ment：把东西放到同一条线上之后的结果。

normal.en: Line is hidden inside align, so alignment always keeps the picture of a straight edge.
normal.cn: align 里面藏着 line，所以 alignment 始终保留「一条直边」的画面。

normal.en: -ment names a result, as in movement and payment, so alignment is what aligning produces.
normal.cn: -ment 表示结果，如 movement、payment，所以 alignment 就是对齐所产生的东西。

normal.en: Physical alignment is of wheels and text; abstract alignment is of aims and policies.
normal.cn: 实物的 alignment 指车轮与文本，抽象的 alignment 指目标与政策。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is in alignment with, not in alignment to.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 in alignment with，不是 in alignment to。

normal.en: Out of alignment means misaligned, whether of a spine or of two departments.
normal.cn: out of alignment 就是没对齐，无论指脊柱还是两个部门。

abstract.en: Picture four wheels all pointing the same way down a straight road.
abstract.cn: 想象四个轮子在一条直路上全都指向同一方向。

abstract.en: Imagine three arrows released at once and flying side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象三支箭同时射出，并排飞行。

abstract.en: Think of two company plans that overlay without a gap.
abstract.cn: 想象两家公司的计划完全重叠，没有一处缝隙。

examples.en: Poor alignment makes the tyres wear unevenly.
examples.cn: 定位不准会让轮胎磨损不均。

examples.en: The policy is in alignment with the new regulations.
examples.cn: 这项政策与新规定保持一致。

examples.en: The planets reached a rare alignment that night.
examples.cn: 那晚行星出现了一次罕见的排列。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿莱恩门特」——阿莱恩（align）是排成线，门特（ment）是结果：排成一条线的结果，就是对齐、一致。

root: 拉丁语 linea「亚麻线、直线」经古法语 ligne 构成法语 aligner「排成一行」，英语借为 align，再加表示结果的后缀 -ment 构成 alignment，字面即「被放到同一条线上的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one straight line applied twice: to objects it means correct position, and to people it means shared direction, so nothing pulls sideways.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一条直线用了两次：用在物体上指位置正确，用在人身上指方向一致，总之没有任何东西往旁边偏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several things pushed onto one straight line
core.cn: 核心意象：把几样东西推到同一条直线上

branches.en: Wheels pointing the same way.
branches.cn: 指向同一方向的四个轮子。

branches.en: Text flush against one margin.
branches.cn: 文本齐整地贴着同一边距。

branches.en: Two boards sharing one goal.
branches.cn: 两个董事会共享一个目标。

branches.en: Countries grouping by interest.
branches.cn: 各国按利益结成群。

branches.en: Both remove sideways pull.
branches.cn: 两者都消除了往旁边的偏力。

intro.en: Alignment is built from a- plus line plus -ment, so the spelling itself shows direction, line and result.
intro.cn: alignment 由 a- 加 line 加 -ment 构成，拼写本身就显示出方向、线与结果。

latinIntro.en: Latin linea, from linum, flax, gave French ligne and aligner; English took align and added -ment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 linea 源自 linum「亚麻」，产生法语 ligne 与 aligner；英语取用 align 并加上 -ment。

items.meaning: the state of being in line

latinEntries.exampleCN: linea 产生 line 与 align。

latinEntries.example: Linum is the plant behind linea.
latinEntries.exampleCN: linum 是 linea 背后的植物。

definition_zh: 碱；（化学）强碱；碱性物质
definition_en: a substance that reacts with acids to form salts, turning litmus blue
core_image: 一杯滑腻的碱水遇到酸便 fizz 着握手言和
scene: 实验室里，蓝色石蕊纸浸进烧杯立刻显出深蓝。The chemist neutralized the acid with a mild alkali.
sceneCN: 这里 alkali 是「碱」（第 1 个义项：与酸反应成盐的化学物质）；句意是化学家用温和的碱中和了酸。

derivatives.zh: alkali 加 -ine，义为「碱性的；含碱的」
alkaline 加 -ity，义为「碱度；碱性」
alkali 加 -oid，义为「生物碱」（如咖啡因）

senses.title: A substance neutralizing acids
senses.definition: a chemical substance that turns litmus blue and neutralizes acids to form salts
senses.definitionCN: 使石蕊变蓝、与酸中和成盐的化学物质
senses.example: Add a little alkali to soften the hard water.
senses.exampleCN: 加一点碱来软化硬水。
senses.why: The Arabic word named the burnt ashes of plants from which the substance was first obtained.
senses.whyCN: 阿拉伯语原词指焚烧植物所得的灰烬，这种物质最初正是从灰中提取的。

senses.title: Alkaline quality or soil
senses.definition: the alkaline character of a solution or land, or such soil itself
senses.definitionCN: 溶液或土地的碱性特征，或这类土壤本身
senses.example: Farmers fought the alkali that whitened their fields.
senses.exampleCN: 农民们与使田地泛白的碱化作斗争。
senses.why: When the white crust on arid land is made of these salts, the substance's name passes to the land itself.
senses.whyCN: 干旱土地上泛白的盐霜正是这类盐分，物质之名便转指土地本身。

intro.en: From Arabic for 'the ashes', carried through medieval Latin into European chemistry.
intro.cn: 源自阿拉伯语「灰烬」，经中世纪拉丁语进入欧洲化学。

items.en: al-qily meant the ashes of the saltwort plant, with the article al- attached.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-qily 指滨藜属植物的灰烬，al- 为定冠词。

items.en: Latin alcali or alkali named the same calcined ashes used in glassmaking.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alcali 指同样的、用于制玻璃的煅烧灰烬。

items.en: Old French alcali passed the word on to English alchemists.
items.cn: 古法语 alcali 把该词传给英语的炼金术士。

items.en: English alkali first meant the ashes and their caustic salts.
items.cn: 14 世纪英语 alkali 最初指灰烬及其苛性盐类。

items.en: Modern chemistry redefined it as bases that neutralize acids; alkali metals, alkaline batteries follow.
items.cn: 现代化学将其定义为中和酸类的碱；碱金属、碱性电池等术语由此派生。

note.en: The first group gathers the Arabic al- family and a look-alike; the second gathers words for bases and salts.
note.cn: 第一组收阿拉伯语 al- 词族与一个形近词；第二组收「碱」与「盐」相关词。

entries.definition: of the nature of an alkali; containing alkali
entries.definitionCN: 碱性的；含碱的

entries.definition: a plant substance like an alkali, such as caffeine
entries.definitionCN: 生物碱（如咖啡因）

entries.definition: a distilled substance; shares only the Arabic article al-
entries.definitionCN: 酒精；仅共享阿拉伯语冠词 al-

entries.definition: to make or become alkaline
entries.definitionCN: 使碱化；碱化

entries.definition: the general chemical term for substances that neutralize acids
entries.definitionCN: 碱；化学上泛指中和酸的物质

entries.definition: a strongly burning alkali such as caustic soda
entries.definitionCN: 苛性物质（如烧碱）

entries.definition: a strong alkaline solution, especially of sodium hydroxide
entries.definitionCN: 碱液（尤指氢氧化钠溶液）

entries.definition: a salt of carbonic acid, often alkaline
entries.definitionCN: 碳酸盐，常呈碱性

entries.definition: the chemical opposite, turning litmus red
entries.definitionCN: 酸；化学对立物，使石蕊变红

normalIntro.en: al- is Arabic 'the'; the root is the burnt ash of a desert plant.
normalIntro.cn: al- 是阿拉伯语定冠词；词根指沙漠植物烧成的灰。

normal.en: Alkali turns litmus paper blue; acid turns it red.
normal.cn: 碱使石蕊变蓝，酸使石蕊变红。

normal.en: Al- words from Arabic: alkali, alcohol, algebra.
normal.cn: 来自阿拉伯语的 al- 词：alkali、alcohol、algebra。

normal.en: alkaline is the adjective; alkaline batteries use it.
normal.cn: alkaline 是形容词；碱性电池就用了它。

normal.en: alkali metals sit at the left edge of the periodic table.
normal.cn: 碱金属位于周期表最左缘。

normal.en: alkaloid = alkali-like plant substance, like caffeine.
normal.cn: alkaloid 意为「似碱的植物物质」，如咖啡因。

abstract.en: Picture grey ashes of burned saltwort heaped in a desert hut.
abstract.cn: 想象沙漠小屋里堆着烧过的滨藜灰。

abstract.en: See a strip of litmus paper turning deep blue in a beaker.
abstract.cn: 想象石蕊纸在烧杯里转为深蓝。

abstract.en: Imagine a white crust creeping across an irrigated field.
abstract.cn: 想象白色盐霜爬满灌溉过的田地。

examples.en: Soap is made by boiling fat with an alkali.
examples.cn: 肥皂是把油脂与碱同煮制成的。

examples.en: The lake water is too alkaline for most fish.
examples.cn: 湖水碱性太强，多数鱼类无法生存。

examples.en: Sodium is the classic alkali metal.
examples.cn: 钠是典型的碱金属。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱靠来」——酸碱相爱靠在一起就中和，碱总等酸来。

root: 阿拉伯语 al-qily「滨藜灰烬」（al- 为定冠词）经中世纪拉丁语 alcali、古法语 alcali 于 14 世纪进入英语，本指煅烧植物灰，现代化学定义为中和酸类的碱。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses spread from the same white powder: the chemical base itself, then the alkaline land it coats.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项由同一把白色粉末展开：先是作为化学碱本身，再是被它覆盖的碱性土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grey plant ashes in a bowl, blue litmus dipped in, fizzing handshake with acid.
core.cn: 核心意象：碗中灰色植物灰烬，石蕊纸浸入变蓝，与酸相遇滋滋中和。

branches.en: soap boiled from fat and ashes
branches.cn: 油脂与灰烬熬成的肥皂

branches.en: sodium flaring at the left edge of the periodic table
branches.cn: 周期表左缘上跃动的钠

branches.en: a whitened field losing its harvest
branches.cn: 泛白失收的田地

branches.en: a brackish lake no fish can live in
branches.cn: 鱼虾绝迹的咸碱湖

branches.en: one ash-born substance, in the beaker and on the land
branches.cn: 同一灰中之物，或在烧杯，或在田土

intro.en: An Arabic article welded to an ash root, with chemistry building its own descendants.
intro.cn: 阿拉伯语冠词焊接在「灰烬」词根上，化学又繁衍出各自的后代。

latinIntro.en: alcali is the medieval Latin form through which the word arrived.
latinIntro.cn: alcali 是该词传入时经由的中世纪拉丁形式。

definition_zh: 指称；声称；（未经证实地）断言；援引作为理由
definition_en: to state that something is true or that someone did something wrong, without proof
core_image: 一个人在文件页脚签下「据称」，把未核实的事推到桌面上
scene: 调查员把一份手写材料放进档案袋，说明材料里提到的细节还没有核实。The complaint alleges that the landlord ignored repeated repair requests.
sceneCN: 这里 allege 指提出尚未证实的说法（第 1 个义项：断言某事为真而尚未举证）；句意为投诉材料称房东无视了多次维修请求。图中可辨识物件：投诉表、档案袋、手写便条、签字笔。

pos.zh: 指称；声称；（未经证实地）断言
（法律）援引、引证作为理由或依据

derivatives.zh: 指控；指称；说法
被指称的；涉嫌的
据称；据说
指称；陈述（古旧用法）

senses.title: State something as true
senses.titleCN: 指称某事为真，尚未举证
senses.definition: to state that something is the case without offering proof
senses.definitionCN: 断言某事确实如此，但未提供证据
senses.example: The complaint alleges that the landlord ignored repeated repair requests.
senses.exampleCN: 投诉材料称房东无视了多次维修请求。
senses.why: Latin allegare meant 'to bring forward, adduce'; a claim is brought forward before the proof that would support it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 allegare 意为「提出、援引」；说法先被提出，支持它的证据后才可能到来。

senses.title: State it in a pleading
senses.titleCN: 在诉状或正式文书中陈述
senses.definition: to set out a fact as true in a legal or official document
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或官方文书中把某项事实陈述为真
senses.example: The plaintiff alleges that the contract was signed under duress.
senses.exampleCN: 原告主张合同是在胁迫下签署的。
senses.why: In pleadings the verb marks a fact the party undertakes to prove, so the legal sense keeps its forward-looking force.
senses.whyCN: 在诉状中，这个动词标出一项当事人承诺日后证明的事实，因此法律义保留了「向前提出」的劲头。

senses.title: Name a person's act
senses.definition: to say that a named person performed a particular act
senses.definitionCN: 指认某个具体的人做过某件具体的事
senses.example: The article alleges that two officials took payments from the contractor.
senses.exampleCN: 文章指称两名官员收受了承包商的款项。
senses.why: The pattern allege that someone did something lets a newspaper name the act while leaving the proof to others.
senses.whyCN: 「指称某人做过某事」这一结构让报纸点明行为，同时把举证留给别人。

senses.title: Cite as a reason
senses.definition: to offer something as a reason, excuse or justification
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物作为理由、借口或正当依据提出
senses.example: He alleged pressure from his superiors as the reason for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 他称上级施加的压力是延误的原因。
senses.why: Adducing a reason is literally bringing something forward, so the same verb serves for excuses and justifications.
senses.whyCN: 提供理由字面上就是把某物提出来，因此同一个动词也能用于借口与辩解。

senses.title: Cite a precedent or text
senses.definition: to quote a case, a rule or a passage in support of an argument
senses.definitionCN: 为支持论点而援引案例、规则或文句
senses.example: Counsel alleged two earlier rulings in support of the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 律师援引了先前两份裁决来支持这一主张。
senses.why: A precedent is also brought forward into an argument, and the old sense of adducing survives in this usage.
senses.whyCN: 先例同样是被提出来放进论证，于是「援引」的旧义在这一用法中留存。

senses.title: Plead in excuse
senses.definition: to plead something as an excuse, an older sense now largely confined to legal and literary texts
senses.definitionCN: 把某事当作辩解提出，这一旧义如今多限于法律与文学文本
senses.example: In the old account he alleged illness and left the assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的记述里，他称病离开了集会。
senses.why: The older sense of adducing a defence survives in legal phrasing, where a party alleges facts to escape liability.
senses.whyCN: 「提出抗辩」的旧义残留在法律措辞里：一方援引事实以摆脱责任。

senses.title: The alleged offender
senses.titleCN: 分词形容词：被指称的，涉嫌的
senses.definition: alleged, as an adjective: named in a claim but not proved guilty
senses.definitionCN: alleged 作形容词：被指称但尚未证实有罪的
senses.example: The alleged offender was never charged.
senses.exampleCN: 被指称的涉案人从未被起诉。
senses.why: The past participle marks a person named in a claim but not yet tried, which is exactly the gap the verb describes.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词标记「被指称却尚未受审」的人，正好对应这个动词所描述的缺口。

senses.title: The reported claim
senses.titleCN: 被动与副词形式：据称、据悉
senses.definition: be alleged to and allegedly: forms that report a claim while keeping the speaker at a distance
senses.definitionCN: 这类转述形式把说法归到他人名下，同时让说话者保持距离
senses.example: The firm is alleged to have moved the money offshore.
senses.exampleCN: 据称该公司把钱转移到了海外。
senses.why: Reported forms are the safest way for a paper to repeat a charge it cannot prove.
senses.whyCN: 对无法举证的指控，转述形式是报纸最稳妥的表达方式。

intro.en: Allege comes through Anglo-French aleger from Latin allegare 'to send forward, adduce', built on ad- 'to' and legare 'to send, depute'. It entered English in the fourteenth century as a pleading verb. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: allege 经盎格鲁—法语 aleger 来自拉丁 allegare「向前送出、援引」，由 ad-「朝向」与 legare「派出、委派」构成，十四世纪作为诉讼用语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Legare meant 'to send as a deputy' and also 'to bequeath'; the root has no connection with law.
items.cn: legare 意为「作为代表派出」，也有「遗赠」义；这个词根与「法律」无关。

items.en: Ad- plus legare gave allegare 'to bring forward, adduce, plead as evidence'.
items.cn: ad- 加 legare 构成 allegare「向前提出、援引、作为证据陈说」。

items.en: Anglo-French aleger carried the legal verb into English courts in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 盎格鲁—法语 aleger 在十四世纪把这个法律动词带入英格兰的法庭。

items.en: In pleading, to allege was to state a fact that the party undertook to prove later.
items.cn: 在诉讼中，allege 指陈述一项当事人承诺日后加以证明的事实。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the verb was used outside court for any claim put forward without proof, and the passive became the reporter's default.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个动词在法庭之外用于任何未经证实而提出的说法，被动式则成了报道的默认写法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the tie between legare and the root of legere 'to gather, choose' is generally thought but not proved; first records are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：一般认为 legare 与 legere「收集、挑选」的词根有关，但未获证实；最早书证为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that share letters or a look with allege but not its root; group two holds verbs of asserting, ranked by how much proof they imply.
note.cn: 第一组是字母或外形与 allege 相近、却不同源的词；第二组是断言类动词，按所含证据分量排列。

entries.definition: From ligare 'to bind', so it means loyalty owed, not a claim made.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ligare「捆绑」，指所负的忠诚，而不是提出的说法。

entries.definition: From legare 'bequeath': what a will or a past age leaves behind.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 legare「遗赠」：遗嘱或过往时代留下的东西。

entries.definition: From legare 'send as a deputy': an official envoy, especially a papal one.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 legare「作为代表派出」：官方使节，尤指教廷使节。

entries.definition: From Greek allegoria 'speaking otherwise'; a story carrying a second meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 allegoria「换个说法」：承载第二层含义的故事。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for saying something is true, with no suggestion that proof is missing.
entries.definitionCN: 说某事为真的日常动词，不暗示缺少证据。

entries.definition: To state something confidently; it stresses the speaker's conviction rather than the lack of proof.
entries.definitionCN: 自信地陈述某事，强调说话者的确信，而非缺少证据。

entries.definition: To say someone did wrong; it always targets a person or body, while allege often targets a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 指某人做错事，总有一个被指对象；而 allege 常指向一件事实。

entries.definition: To argue that something is true as part of a dispute, implying opposing views.
entries.definitionCN: 在争论中主张某事为真，暗示存在对立观点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ad- 'to' plus legare 'send': a claim sent forward for others to test.
normal.cn: ad-「朝向」加 legare「送」：把说法送到别人面前去检验。

normal.en: The family runs allege, allegation, alleged, allegedly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 allege、allegation、alleged 与 allegedly。

normal.en: News prose prefers the passive: the company is alleged to have...
normal.cn: 新闻语体偏爱被动式：据称该公司曾……

normal.en: A pleading alleges facts; the other side then admits or denies them.
normal.cn: 诉状提出事实主张，随后由对方承认或否认。

normal.en: Allegiance is a false friend from the binding root, not from sending.
normal.cn: allegiance 是假朋友，来自「捆绑」的词根，与「送出」无关。

abstract.en: Picture a claim pushed through a door before anyone checks who is behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个说法被推进门里，却没人先确认门后是谁。

abstract.en: Picture a signature at the foot of a page that nobody has read to the end.
abstract.cn: 想象一页没人读完的文件，页脚已经有了签名。

abstract.en: Picture a label reading reported stuck to a parcel nobody has opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一只贴着「据报」标签、却没人拆开过的包裹。

examples.en: The study alleges a link between the two chemicals and the illness.
examples.cn: 这项研究称这两种化学品与那种疾病存在关联。

examples.en: It was alleged that the files had been destroyed before the hearing.
examples.cn: 据称档案在听证之前就已被销毁。

examples.en: She alleged no reason for the delay and simply left.
examples.cn: 她没有给出延误的任何理由，就此离开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a + lege（送出）」——话先送出去，证据后再补：指称、声称

root: 拉丁 allegare「向前提出、援引」= ad-（朝向）+ legare「派出、送出」；英语 allege 经盎格鲁—法语 aleger 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one move: a claim is sent forward, then the settings change from court to newspaper to quotation, and finally to the grammatical forms that report it at arm's length.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：说法先被送出去，接着场景从法庭换到报纸再到引证，最后落在把那项说法隔开距离转述的语法形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone signs the word reported at the foot of a page and pushes the unverified sheet across the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人在页脚签下「据称」，把未核实的纸推到桌子对面。

branches.en: THE CLAIM SENT: the same move serves a newspaper sentence and a formal pleading.
branches.cn: 送出的说法：同一个动作既用于报纸句子，也用于正式诉状。

branches.en: THE ACT NAMED: a person and a deed are specified, while the proof stays elsewhere.
branches.cn: 点明的行为：指出具体的人与具体的事，证据却留在别处。

branches.en: THE REASON ADDUCED: a pressure, a precedent or a passage is brought forward in support.
branches.cn: 援引的理由：把压力、先例或文句提出来充当依据。

branches.en: THE OLD DEFENCE: pleading illness or some other fact to escape a duty belongs to an older legal idiom.
branches.cn: 古老的辩解：称病或以其他事实脱责，属于更早的法律习语。

branches.en: THE REPORTED FORM: the participle and the adverb let a writer repeat a charge without owning it.
branches.cn: 转述形式：分词与副词让写作者重复一项指控，却不必替它担保。

intro.en: Allege is a Latin verb whose prefix, root and suffixes each build other English words.
intro.cn: allege 是一个拉丁动词，前缀、词根与后缀各自还构成别的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin legare gives legate, legacy and legation; allege and allegation come from allegare, where ad- adds direction. Allegiance belongs to the binding root and not here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 legare 衍生 legate、legacy 与 legation；allege 与 allegation 出自 allegare，由 ad- 增添方向义。allegiance 属于「捆绑」词根，不在这一族。

items.structure: ad- (Latin prefix, assimilated to al- before l)
items.example: The prefix pushes the claim into view.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把说法推到人前。
这个词根提供「送出」的意思。

items.meaning: to bring forward as a claim
items.example: The report alleges that the forms were altered.
items.exampleCN: 报告指称这些表格被改动过。

items.example: The alleged theft was never reported.
items.exampleCN: 被指称的盗窃从未有人报案。

items.example: The clerk allegedly deleted the file.
items.exampleCN: 据称那名职员删除了文件。

items.example: The legation closed in the spring.
items.exampleCN: 那个公使馆在春天关闭了。

items.example: The legate carried a sealed letter.
items.exampleCN: 使节带着一封密封的信。

definition_zh: 过敏的；对……过敏的；对……极反感的
definition_en: having a physical reaction to a substance, or strongly disliking something
core_image: 皮肤上突然浮起的红点，一碰到花粉就发痒
scene: 春天花粉飞扬，她一出门就不停打喷嚏。She is allergic to pollen and sneezes all through spring.
sceneCN: 这里 allergic 是「过敏的」（第 1 个义项：对某物质产生身体过敏反应）；句意为她对花粉过敏，整个春天都在打喷嚏。

pos.zh: 形容词：过敏的；对……极反感的

derivatives.zh: 去掉形容词后缀得到的基础名词，义为「过敏」
由 allergy 加 -gen 构成，义为「过敏原」
由 allergy 加 -ist 构成，义为「过敏科医生」
由 allergen 加 -ic 构成，义为「引起过敏的」

senses.title: Reacting physically to a substance
senses.definition: having an immune reaction such as sneezing, itching, or swelling after contact with a particular substance
senses.definitionCN: 接触某种特定物质后出现打喷嚏、发痒或肿胀等免疫反应
senses.example: My brother is allergic to peanuts.
senses.exampleCN: 我弟弟对花生过敏。
senses.why: Greek allos meant other and ergon meant work; allergy named the body working against an otherwise harmless other thing.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 allos 意为「别的」，ergon 意为「工作」；allergy 命名身体对一种本来无害的「他者」发起抵抗工作。

senses.title: Strongly disliking something
senses.definition: strongly averse to something, often in a humorous or emphatic way
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物强烈反感，常带幽默或强调语气
senses.example: He is allergic to meetings that last all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他对开一下午的会深恶痛绝。
senses.why: The body's rejection of a substance becomes a metaphor for the mind's rejection of an idea, and the reaction is equally automatic.
senses.whyCN: 身体对物质的排斥，被借喻为头脑对观念的排斥，而且反应同样自动。

senses.title: Caused by allergy
senses.definition: describing a disease or symptom produced by an allergic reaction
senses.definitionCN: 形容由过敏反应引起的疾病或症状
senses.example: The clinic treats children with allergic asthma.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所治疗患过敏性哮喘的儿童。
senses.why: In medical compounds the word marks cause rather than the sufferer: the asthma is not allergic, it is asthma caused by allergy.
senses.whyCN: 在医学复合词里，这个词标的是病因而不是患者：哮喘本身不过敏，而是由过敏引起的哮喘。

intro.en: Allergic is a twentieth-century medical coinage built from two Greek words and later borrowed by everyday speech.
intro.cn: allergic 是二十世纪的医学新造词，由两个希腊词构成，后来被日常语言借用。

items.en: Greek allos meant other or different, the first half of the coinage.
items.cn: 希腊语 allos 意为「别的、不同的」，是新造词的前半部分。

items.en: Greek ergon meant work or action, and it also gives English energy and ergonomic.
items.cn: 希腊语 ergon 意为工作或作用，也是英语 energy 与 ergonomic 的来源。

items.en: The physician Clemens von Pirquet coined allergy for the body's altered, over-reactive response to a foreign substance.
items.cn: 医生克莱门斯·冯·皮尔凯造出 allergy 一词，指身体对外来物质的改变了的过度反应。

items.en: English borrowed allergy in the early twentieth century as the medical term spread.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，随着医学术语传播，英语借入了 allergy。

items.en: The adjective allergic followed, formed with the Latin-derived suffix -ic.
items.cn: 形容词 allergic 随后出现，用源自拉丁语的 -ic 构成。

items.en: Later the word was extended to strong dislike, first in speech and then in dictionaries.
items.cn: 后来这个词被扩展到强烈反感，先出现在口语，再进入词典。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the allergy family; the near-meaning group gathers words for sensitivity and intolerance.
note.cn: 形近组收 allergy 词族；近义组收表示敏感与不耐受的词。

entries.definition: The medical condition behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指形容词背后的医学状况，即过敏。

entries.definition: A substance that triggers an allergic reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 指引发过敏反应的物质，即过敏原。

entries.definition: A doctor who treats allergies.
entries.definitionCN: 指治疗过敏的医生。

entries.definition: Able to cause an allergic reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够引起过敏反应的。

entries.definition: Reacting easily to a substance or situation, a broader word.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某物质或情境容易起反应，是更宽泛的词。

entries.definition: Unable to digest or accept a food or substance.
entries.definitionCN: 指无法消化或接受某种食物或物质。

entries.definition: Reacting more strongly than usual to a stimulus.
entries.definitionCN: 指对刺激的反应比平常更强烈。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek meaning other work and the visible signs of a reaction.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用希腊语「他者 + 工作」的含义，以及看得见的反应迹象。

normal.en: Allergy is other work: the body works against something that should be harmless.
normal.cn: allergy 是「他者的工作」：身体对本来无害的东西发起抵抗。

normal.en: Allergic to pollen means pollen starts that work, and the nose pays.
normal.cn: allergic to pollen 意为花粉启动这项工作，鼻子付出代价。

normal.en: Allergic reaction is the body's overreaction, not the substance's attack.
normal.cn: allergic reaction 是身体的过度反应，而不是物质的攻击。

normal.en: Allergic asthma is asthma caused by allergy, so read the compound from right to left.
normal.cn: allergic asthma 是由过敏引起的哮喘，所以要从右往左读这个复合词。

normal.en: Saying you are allergic to meetings borrows the body's automatic refusal for the mind.
normal.cn: 说自己对开会有过敏反应，是把身体的自动拒绝借给头脑使用。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet house where a harmless cat walks in, and every alarm in the walls goes off.
abstract.cn: 想象一间安静的屋子，一只无害的猫走进来，墙里所有警报同时响起。

abstract.en: Nothing in the cat changed; only the house's way of working changed.
abstract.cn: 猫没有变，变的只是屋子运作的方式。

abstract.en: Allergic is the name of that house, not the name of the cat.
abstract.cn: allergic 是那间屋子的名字，不是那只猫的名字。

examples.en: She is allergic to shellfish and carries medicine with her.
examples.cn: 她对贝类过敏，随身带着药。

examples.en: The doctor asked whether anyone in the family was allergic.
examples.cn: 医生问家里是否有人过敏。

examples.en: He is allergic to loud arguments in small rooms.
examples.cn: 他对小房间里的高声争吵极为反感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额了叽刻」——额，一碰花粉就叽叽刻刻打喷嚏，过敏了

root: 由希腊语 allos（别的、不同的）与 ergon（工作、作用）构成；一九零六年由医生皮尔凯造出 allergy，指身体对外来物质的过度反应，再加 -ic 构成形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses describe the body's reaction and the illness it causes; one extends the reaction to the mind's strong dislike.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项描述身体的反应与由此引起的疾病；一个义项把这种反应延伸到头脑的强烈反感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a harmless substance enters the body, and the body's defences treat it as an invader.
core.cn: 核心意象：一种无害物质进入身体，身体的防线却把它当作入侵者。

branches.en: THE OTHER: Greek allos marks the substance as foreign, and the body reacts to its foreignness.
branches.cn: 他者线：希腊语 allos 标出物质的外来性，身体正是对这种外来性起反应。

branches.en: THE WORK: ergon is the body's work, and allergy is that work turned against something harmless.
branches.cn: 工作线：ergon 是身体的运作，过敏就是这项运作反过来对付无害之物。

branches.en: THE DISEASE: medical compounds use the word to mark a cause, as in allergic asthma.
branches.cn: 疾病线：医学复合词用这个词标出病因，如过敏性哮喘。

branches.en: THE MIND: the body's automatic refusal becomes a metaphor for strong dislike.
branches.cn: 头脑线：身体的自动拒绝变成强烈反感的比喻。

branches.en: THE REFLEX: in both senses the reaction is fast and not chosen.
branches.cn: 反射线：无论哪个义项，反应都很快且非自愿。

intro.en: Allergic is a Greek-based medical word with a Latin-style adjective ending and a productive family around allergy.
intro.cn: allergic 是希腊词基的医学词，带拉丁式形容词词尾，并围绕 allergy 有能产词族。

latinIntro.en: The roots are Greek rather than Latin, so the Latin entries are limited to the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 词根来自希腊语而非拉丁语，因此拉丁条目只限形容词词尾。

items.example: It is the first half of allergy.
items.exampleCN: 它是 allergy 的前半部分。

items.example: It is the second half of allergy.
items.exampleCN: 它是 allergy 的后半部分。

items.meaning: the body's response to an allergen
items.example: The rash was an allergic reaction.

definition_zh: 过敏；过敏反应；（口语）反感
definition_en: a condition in which the immune system reacts too strongly to a harmless substance such as pollen or food; informally, a strong dislike
core_image: 身体把无害的东西当成敌人猛打
scene: 她小时候喝牛奶没事，成年后一喝就起疹子。Her allergy to dairy appeared only in adulthood.
sceneCN: 这里 allergy 是「过敏」（第 1 个义项：免疫系统对某种物质产生过度反应）；句意为她对乳制品的过敏到成年后才出现。核心画面是身体把无害的东西当成敌人猛打。

derivatives.zh: 相关形容词，义为「过敏的；反感的」
加 -gen 构成，义为「过敏原」
加 -ist 构成，义为「过敏专科医生」

senses.title: An immune overreaction
senses.definition: a condition in which the immune system reacts too strongly to a harmless substance such as pollen, food or dust
senses.definitionCN: 免疫系统对花粉、食物或灰尘等无害物质反应过强的状态
senses.example: Her allergy makes her eyes water every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 她的过敏让她每年春天都流泪。
senses.why: Allergy was coined from Greek allos, other, plus ergon, work: the body does a changed work, reacting to something it should ignore.
senses.whyCN: allergy 由希腊语 allos「其他」加 ergon「作用」造出：身体做了一种改变的作用，对本该忽略的东西起了反应。

senses.title: A strong personal dislike
senses.definition: an informal dislike of a thing or activity, used humorously as in an allergy to hard work
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物或活动的非正式厌恶，常带幽默色彩，如说对辛苦工作「过敏」
senses.example: He claims an allergy to any meeting before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称对中午之前的任何会议都过敏。
senses.why: The medical image is borrowed for taste: the person reacts as strongly and as involuntarily as if the thing were a real allergen.
senses.whyCN: 这里把医学意象借用来表达好恶：这个人的反应同样强烈、同样不由自主，仿佛那东西真是过敏原。

intro.en: Allergy is a coined medical word: Greek allos, other, plus ergon, work, named an altered reaction, and a Viennese doctor turned it into a noun in the early twentieth century.
intro.cn: allergy 是一个被造出来的医学词：希腊语 allos「其他」加 ergon「作用」表示「改变了的反应」，一位维也纳医生在二十世纪初把它变成名词。

items.en: Greek allos meant other or different, the root behind allegory and allopathy.
items.cn: 希腊语 allos 意为「其他、不同」，是 allegory 与 allopathy 背后的词根。

items.en: Greek ergon meant work or action, the root of energy, organ and synergy.
items.cn: 希腊语 ergon 意为「作用、工作」，是 energy、organ 与 synergy 的词根。

items.en: The Viennese paediatrician Clemens von Pirquet coined Allergie in the early twentieth century to name any altered immune reactivity.
items.cn: 维也纳儿科医生克莱门斯·冯·皮尔凯在二十世纪初造出 Allergie，用以指任何改变了的免疫反应性。

items.en: English borrowed allergy within a few years, and it quickly replaced older phrases describing unusual reactions to food.
items.cn: 英语没几年就借入 allergy，很快取代了描述「对食物异常反应」的旧说法。

items.en: Today allergy covers both the clinical condition and a joking dislike, with allergic and allergen built from the same stem.
items.cn: 如今 allergy 既指临床病症，也指玩笑式的反感，allergic 与 allergen 都建立在同一词干上。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the allerg- family; the near-meaning group lists other words for a bad reaction to a substance.
note.cn: 形近组保留 allerg- 词族；近义组列出其他表示「对物质产生不良反应」的词。

entries.definition: Having an allergy, or strongly averse.
entries.definitionCN: 过敏的，或强烈反感的。

entries.definition: A substance that triggers an allergy.
entries.definitionCN: 引发过敏的物质。

entries.definition: A doctor specialising in allergies.
entries.definitionCN: 过敏专科医生。

entries.definition: A comparison between similar things.
entries.definitionCN: 相似事物之间的比较。

entries.definition: An excessive immune response.
entries.definitionCN: 过度的免疫反应。

entries.definition: Inability to tolerate a food or substance.
entries.definitionCN: 无法耐受某种食物或物质。

entries.definition: A tendency to react strongly.
entries.definitionCN: 容易起强烈反应的倾向。

entries.definition: A strong dislike of something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物的强烈厌恶。

normalIntro.en: Allergy is allo, other, plus erg, work: the body working differently on a harmless thing.
normalIntro.cn: allergy 就是 allo「其他」加 erg「作用」：身体对无害的东西起了不一样的作用。

normal.en: Allergic is the adjective, allergen the trigger, allergy the condition.
normal.cn: allergic 是形容词，allergen 是诱因，allergy 是病症。

normal.en: Say an allergy to nuts, not an allergy of nuts: the preposition is to.
normal.cn: 说 an allergy to nuts，不说 an allergy of nuts：介词用 to。

normal.en: It is countable, so say two allergies, one to pollen and one to cats.
normal.cn: 它可数，所以说 two allergies，一个对花粉，一个对猫。

normal.en: Food intolerance is not an allergy: it does not involve the immune system.
normal.cn: 食物不耐受不是过敏：它不涉及免疫系统。

normal.en: The joking use keeps to as well, as in an allergy to paperwork.
normal.cn: 玩笑用法同样用 to，如 an allergy to paperwork。

abstract.en: Picture an army attacking a delivery of flour as if it were an invasion.
abstract.cn: 想象一支军队把一车面粉当成入侵来攻打。

abstract.en: Imagine a door alarm that rings every time a friend knocks.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门铃警报，每次朋友敲门都响。

abstract.en: Think of a bodyguard who tackles the postman.
abstract.cn: 想象一个保镖把邮递员扑倒在地。

examples.en: The label warns that the sauce may cause an allergy.
examples.cn: 标签警告这种酱汁可能引发过敏。

examples.en: She outgrew her childhood allergy to eggs.
examples.cn: 她长大后不再对鸡蛋过敏。

examples.en: His allergy to criticism makes feedback painful.
examples.cn: 他对批评的「过敏」让反馈变得难受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿勒吉」——阿勒（aller）是「别的」，吉（gy）是「作用」：身体对别的东西起了作用，就是过敏。

root: 希腊语 allos「其他、不同」加 ergon「作用」构成「改变了的反应」这一概念，二十世纪初由维也纳医生造为德语 Allergie，英语借入成为 allergy，字面即「对无害之物起了别样作用」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are an overreaction to something harmless: the medical one is the immune system attacking pollen or food, and the joking one is a person recoiling from work or criticism.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是对无害之物的过度反应：医学义是免疫系统攻击花粉或食物，玩笑义是人对工作或批评避之不及。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the body attacking a harmless visitor
core.cn: 核心意象：身体攻击一个无害的来客

branches.en: Pollen treated as an invader.
branches.cn: 花粉被当成入侵者。

branches.en: Skin rising in rash after a meal.
branches.cn: 饭后皮肤起疹。

branches.en: A person dodging every extra task.
branches.cn: 一个人躲开每一项额外任务。

branches.en: A joke about hating early meetings.
branches.cn: 一句讨厌早会的玩笑。

branches.en: Both react too strongly to too little.
branches.cn: 两者都对太小的刺激反应太强。

intro.en: Allergy joins two Greek roots, allo- for other and erg- for work, and the same stem then builds allergic, allergen and allergist.
intro.cn: allergy 拼合两个希腊词根：allo-「其他」与 erg-「作用」，同一词干随后造出 allergic、allergen 与 allergist。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin layer: Greek allos and ergon were joined directly, coined in German, and then borrowed into English.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁语层次：希腊语 allos 与 ergon 直接拼合，先在德语中造出，再进入英语。

definition_zh: 减轻；缓解；缓和；使缓和
definition_en: to make pain, difficulty or a bad feeling less severe without removing its cause
core_image: 压在人肩上的石袋被一只只手卸下一半，肩线慢慢回正
scene: 换药时最疼，护士引导病人慢慢呼吸，疼痛就退了一些。The clinic uses guided breathing to alleviate pain during dressing changes.
sceneCN: 这里指让疼痛变轻（第 1 个义项：减轻疼痛或症状）；句意为诊所靠引导呼吸来缓解换药时的疼痛。图中可辨识物件：病床、绷带、被卸下一半的石袋。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「减轻；缓解」
由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「缓解性的」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「缓解的；缓和剂」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「缓解者；缓解手段」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已减轻的」

senses.title: To ease pain
senses.definition: to reduce the intensity of physical pain without curing its cause
senses.definitionCN: 降低身体疼痛的强度，但不消除病因
senses.example: The drug alleviates pain but does not repair the joint.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药能减轻疼痛，却修不好关节。
senses.why: Alleviate comes from a word for light, and pain is treated as a weight that can be made lighter.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自「轻」义，疼痛被当作一份可以变轻的重量。

senses.title: To ease pressure or strain
senses.definition: to reduce the level of stress, workload or tension that people or systems carry
senses.definitionCN: 降低人或系统所承受的压力、工作量或紧张程度
senses.example: Extra staff alleviated the pressure on the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 增加人手缓解了夜班的压力。
senses.why: Pressure is a load, so making it lighter is the same physical move applied to work.
senses.whyCN: 压力是负荷，让它变轻就是把同一物理动作用到工作上。

senses.title: To reduce poverty or hardship
senses.definition: to lessen the severity of material hardship, usually by policy rather than by cure
senses.definitionCN: 减轻物质困苦的严重程度，通常靠政策而非根治
senses.example: The subsidy alleviated hardship among the poorest households.
senses.exampleCN: 这项补贴缓解了最贫困家庭的困苦。
senses.why: Social policy speaks of lightening a burden that cannot yet be removed.
senses.whyCN: 社会政策谈的是先把卸不掉的负担弄轻。

senses.title: To relieve congestion
senses.definition: to make traffic, queues or demand less dense
senses.definitionCN: 使交通、排队或需求不再那么密集
senses.example: A second entrance alleviated congestion at the main gate.
senses.exampleCN: 增加第二个入口缓解了正门的拥堵。
senses.why: Congestion is pressure concentrated at one point, and the verb spreads or lowers it.
senses.whyCN: 拥堵是集中在一处的压力，这个动词把它摊开或降低。

senses.title: To soothe anxiety
senses.definition: to make fear or worry less intense, often temporarily
senses.definitionCN: 使恐惧或担忧不那么强烈，常常只是暂时
senses.example: A clear explanation alleviated her anxiety about the results.
senses.exampleCN: 清楚的解释缓解了她对结果的焦虑。
senses.why: Emotional weight is lightened much as physical weight is, which is why the same verb serves both.
senses.whyCN: 情绪的重量与身体的重量一样可以被减轻，所以同一个动词两者都管。

senses.title: To soften an impact
senses.definition: to reduce how hard an event, change or policy hits those affected
senses.definitionCN: 降低某个事件、变化或政策对受影响者的打击力度
senses.example: The fund alleviated the impact of the sudden price rise.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔基金缓和了价格骤涨带来的冲击。
senses.why: An impact lands as force, and lightening it is to take part of the blow away.
senses.whyCN: 冲击以力量的形式落下，减轻它就是卸掉一部分打击。

senses.title: To provide relief measures
senses.definition: to supply practical help that makes a difficult situation easier to bear
senses.definitionCN: 提供实际帮助，使困难处境更容易承受
senses.example: The city alleviated the water shortage with temporary deliveries.
senses.exampleCN: 市里用临时送水缓解了缺水。
senses.why: Here the verb shifts from the feeling to the measure that produces the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词从「感受」转向「产生该感受的措施」。

senses.title: To treat symptoms only
senses.definition: to give symptomatic relief while leaving the underlying condition untreated
senses.definitionCN: 只提供症状层面的缓解，不处理根本病因
senses.example: Hospice care alleviated her symptoms without treating the disease itself.
senses.exampleCN: 临终照护缓解了她的症状，却没有治疗疾病本身。
senses.why: Medicine distinguishes cure from relief, and alleviate belongs firmly to the second.
senses.whyCN: 医学区分「治愈」与「缓解」，这个词稳稳属于后者。

intro.en: Alleviate comes from Latin alleviare, to lighten, from ad, toward, and levare, to raise or lighten, from levis, light in weight. It is not related to the Latin verb for raising or nourishing.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 alleviare「使轻」，由 ad「向」与 levare「举起、减轻」构成，而 levare 出自 levis「轻」；它与拉丁语中表示「举起、养育」的另一个动词无关。

items.en: Levis meant light in weight, and the same root gives levity, elevate and relief through related verbs.
items.cn: 这个词指重量轻；同一词根经相关动词还给出「轻快」「举起」与「缓解」等词。

items.en: Levare meant to lighten or to raise, and the two readings share the picture of something becoming easier to lift.
items.cn: 这个词意为使轻或举起，两种读法共享「东西变得容易举起」的画面。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant toward, and it marks the direction in which the lightening is applied.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「向」，标出减轻作用的方向。

items.en: Alleviare meant to lighten, relieve or comfort, and it was used of pain, grief and burdens.
items.cn: 这个词意为使轻、缓解、安慰，用于疼痛、悲伤与负担。

items.en: It is often confused with allevare, to raise or feed, but the two verbs differ in root and meaning.
items.cn: 它常与表示「举起、喂养」的 allevare 混淆，但两者词根与词义都不同。

items.en: English took the verb directly from Latin in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪直接从拉丁语引入这个动词，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the light root or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of relief and reduction.
note.cn: 第一组与「alleviate」共享「轻」的词根或只是形近；第二组是与「缓解、减少」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of making something less severe.
entries.definitionCN: 指减轻、缓解这一行为的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for something that relieves.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指起缓解作用的。

entries.definition: To raise something, from the same light root through a different prefix path.
entries.definitionCN: 指举起、抬高；同出「轻」词根，经不同前缀路径。

entries.definition: Lightness of mood, literally lightness of weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指情绪轻快，字面就是「重量轻」。

entries.definition: The noun for easing a burden, from a related Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指负担的减轻，出自相关的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To take a burden or pain away, often more completely than alleviate.
entries.definitionCN: 指卸去负担或疼痛，程度常比 alleviate 更彻底。

entries.definition: To make something less painful or difficult, in plain everyday language.
entries.definitionCN: 指使不那么痛苦或困难，是日常说法。

entries.definition: To make something bad less severe, especially damage or risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指使坏事不那么严重，尤指损害或风险。

entries.definition: To calm a feeling or a surface, with a comforting tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指安抚情绪或舒缓表面，带安慰色彩。

entries.definition: To make or become smaller in amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指在数量上减少。

entries.definition: To bring down a size, amount or level, the broad neutral verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指降低大小、数量或水平，是宽泛中性的说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the light root, the false twin allevare, and the medical phrases that keep the word in use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「轻」的词根、容易混淆的近形动词 allevare，以及让这个词保持活力的医学搭配。

normal.en: Levis is light, so alleviate is to put something on a scale and watch the reading drop.
normal.cn: levis 是「轻」，所以这个词就是把东西放上秤，看读数往下走。

normal.en: Elevate and alleviate look alike and are related, but one raises and the other lightens.
normal.cn: elevate 与 alleviate 形近且同源，但一个往上举，一个往轻里减。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with allevare, which meant to raise or feed.
normal.cn: 不要与 allevare 混淆，那个词是「举起、喂养」。

normal.en: Clinics alleviate pain, cities alleviate congestion, and policy alleviates poverty.
normal.cn: 诊所缓解疼痛，城市缓解拥堵，政策缓解贫困。

normal.en: Alleviate treats the symptom; cure treats the cause.
normal.cn: 这个词处理症状，「治愈」处理病因。

abstract.en: To alleviate is to admit you cannot remove the weight, and still take some of it off.
abstract.cn: 减轻，就是承认重量卸不掉，却仍然拿走一部分。

abstract.en: Relief is not cure: the stone is lighter, but it is still on the shoulder.
abstract.cn: 缓解不是治愈：石头变轻了，可还在肩上。

abstract.en: Every soothing act is a small redistribution of weight from the weak to the strong.
abstract.cn: 每一次安抚，都是把重量从弱者身上往强者身上挪一点。

examples.en: Cool compresses alleviate the itching for about an hour.
examples.cn: 冷敷能缓解瘙痒大约一小时。

examples.en: The new lane alleviated congestion on the western approach.
examples.cn: 新车道缓解了西侧入口的拥堵。

examples.en: Cash transfers alleviated hardship but did not end it.
examples.cn: 现金补助缓解了困苦，却没有终结它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿利维特」——肩上的石袋被卸下一半：减轻、缓解

root: 拉丁语 levis「轻」→ levare「使轻、举起」→ alleviare「使轻、缓解」（ad-「向」）；英语十六世纪直接引入。与表示「举起、养育」的 allevare 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all lighten something: pain, pressure, poverty, congestion, anxiety, impact, shortage and symptoms.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在给某物减重：疼痛、压力、贫困、拥堵、焦虑、冲击、短缺与症状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: half the stones are lifted off a shoulder, and the shoulder slowly straightens.
core.cn: 核心意象：肩上的石袋被卸下一半，肩线慢慢回正。

branches.en: THE BODY IS LIGHTENED: pain or a symptom loses intensity, though the cause may remain.
branches.cn: 身体变轻：疼痛或症状减弱，病因却可能还在。

branches.en: THE LOAD IS SHARED: stress and workload are lowered for those carrying them.
branches.cn: 负荷被分担：承受者的压力与工作量降下来。

branches.en: THE INWARD WEIGHT: hardship and anxiety become easier to bear.
branches.cn: 内心的重量：困苦与焦虑变得较易承受。

branches.en: THE CROWD IS SPREAD: congestion loses its concentration at one point.
branches.cn: 人群被摊开：拥堵失去那一点上的集中。

branches.en: THE BLOW IS SOFTENED: an impact or a shortage meets a measure that takes part of its force.
branches.cn: 打击被软化：冲击或短缺遇上一项卸去部分力度的措施。

intro.en: Alleviate is a Latin verb built from a light root, and the same root runs through elevate, levity and relief.
intro.cn: 这是一个由「轻」词根构成的拉丁动词，同一词根贯穿 elevate、levity 与 relief。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies levis, levare and alleviare; the deeper origin of the root is reconstructed rather than recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 levis、levare、alleviare；词根更早的来源属重构而非有记录的形式。

items.example: The adjective named what is easy to carry.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指容易携带的东西。

items.example: The two readings meet in the idea of making something easier to lift.
items.exampleCN: 两种读法在「让东西更容易举起」处汇合。

items.example: Before l it assimilates to al-, as in alleviate.
items.exampleCN: 在 l 前同化为 al-，即 alleviate 的形式。

items.example: The verb was used of pain and grief.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词用于疼痛与悲伤。

items.example: The same root, moved from weight to temperament.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根，从重量移到性情。

由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「缓解性的」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「缓解的；缓和剂」

definition_zh: 小巷；窄街；小径；保龄球道；死胡同
definition_en: a narrow passage between buildings, a bowling lane, or a garden path
core_image: 两堵高墙夹出的一条窄缝，尽头才见一点光
scene: 孩子把球滚进两栋楼之间的窄巷，转身就跑。The cat dashed into a narrow alley between the two buildings.
sceneCN: 这里 alley 是「小巷」（第 1 个义项：建筑之间的狭窄通道）；句意为猫冲进两栋楼之间的窄巷。

pos.zh: 名词：小巷；窄街；小径；保龄球道

derivatives.zh: 由 alley 与 way 构成的复合名词，义为「小巷；窄道」
复合名词，义为「流浪猫」，指在巷子里讨生活的猫
复合名词，义为「保龄球馆」或「保龄球道」
复合名词，义为「死胡同」，也比喻没有前途的办法

senses.title: A narrow passage between buildings
senses.definition: a narrow street or passage running between or behind buildings
senses.definitionCN: 在建筑物之间或后方延伸的狭窄街道或通道
senses.example: They met in an alley behind the market.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在市场后面的一条小巷里见面。
senses.why: Old French alee meant a walking or a passage, from the verb to go; an alley is a route squeezed between walls.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 alee 意为行走或通道，来自表示「走」的动词；alley 就是被墙夹出来的一条路线。

senses.title: A bowling lane
senses.definition: the long narrow track down which a bowling ball is rolled
senses.definitionCN: 供保龄球滚向球瓶的长而窄的球道
senses.example: The ball curved across the alley and hit the last pin.
senses.exampleCN: 球斜穿过球道，击中了最后一只瓶。
senses.why: A bowling lane has exactly the shape of an alley: a long narrow strip with walls or gutters on both sides.
senses.whyCN: 保龄球道的形状正像一条小巷：长而窄，两侧有边沟或挡板。

senses.title: A garden path
senses.definition: a narrow path in a garden or park, often bordered by plants
senses.definitionCN: 花园或公园中的狭窄小径，常由植物镶边
senses.example: A gravel alley led from the gate to the roses.
senses.exampleCN: 一条碎石小径从门口通向玫瑰丛。
senses.why: The passage does not need buildings: any narrow way meant for walking can carry the name.
senses.whyCN: 通道不一定需要建筑：任何供人行走的窄路都能用这个名字。

senses.title: A blind alley: no way forward
senses.definition: a course of action that leads nowhere, from the image of a passage with no exit
senses.definitionCN: 指走不通的做法，来自没有出口的通道这一意象
senses.example: Endless testing was a blind alley for the research team.
senses.exampleCN: 无止境的测试对研究团队来说是条死胡同。
senses.why: A real alley can end at a wall; the mind borrows that wall for any plan that cannot continue.
senses.whyCN: 真实的小巷可以在墙前终止；头脑把那堵墙借给任何无法继续的计划。

intro.en: Alley comes from a French verb meaning to go, and its narrow shape then spread to bowling and to dead ends.
intro.cn: alley 来自一个意为「走」的法语动词，它狭窄的形状随后延伸到保龄球与死胡同。

items.en: Latin ambulare meant to walk about, and it is the distant source of alley and of amble.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ambulare 意为到处走动，是 alley 与 amble 的远源。

items.en: Old French aler meant to go, and its participle alee named a going or a passage.
items.cn: 古法语 aler 意为去、走，其分词形式 alee 指一次行走或一条通道。

items.en: Middle English took the word as aley, a narrow way for walking.
items.cn: 中世纪英语借入作 aley，指供行走的窄路。

items.en: The long narrow lane of a bowling game borrowed the shape and the name.
items.cn: 保龄球那长而窄的球道借用了这个形状，也借用了这个名字。

items.en: Garden paths used the word for any narrow walk bordered by plants.
items.cn: 花园小径用这个词指任何由植物镶边的窄走道。

items.en: The phrase blind alley extended the physical dead end into a failed plan.
items.cn: 短语 blind alley 把物理上的死胡同延伸到失败的计划。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers alley compounds; the near-meaning group gathers narrow ways and passages.
note.cn: 形近组收 alley 的复合词；近义组收狭窄的道路与通道。

entries.definition: A narrow passage, often between buildings.
entries.definitionCN: 指狭窄通道，常在建筑之间。

entries.definition: A stray cat that lives in streets and alleys.
entries.definitionCN: 指在街巷里生活的流浪猫。

entries.definition: A building or lane for bowling.
entries.definitionCN: 指打保龄球的场馆或球道。

entries.definition: A passage with no exit, or a plan that cannot succeed.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有出口的通道，或无法成功的计划。

entries.definition: A narrow road in the country or a marked strip of a wider road.
entries.definitionCN: 指乡间窄路，或宽路上划出的一条车道。

entries.definition: A way through or along which someone or something passes.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或物穿行而过的通道。

entries.definition: A track made by walking, often outdoors.
entries.definitionCN: 指走出来的小路，多在户外。

entries.definition: A long passage inside a building or between rooms.
entries.definitionCN: 指建筑内部或房间之间的长通道。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with the narrow gap and then stretch it into a bowling lane and a dead end.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子先抓住那条窄缝，再把它拉成保龄球道与死胡同。

normal.en: Alley is a walking passage squeezed between two walls, so narrowness is the core.
normal.cn: alley 是被两堵墙夹出来的行走通道，所以「窄」是核心。

normal.en: A bowling alley is an alley laid flat and given pins.
normal.cn: bowling alley 是把小巷放平，再摆上球瓶。

normal.en: A garden alley is the same narrow walk with flowers instead of walls.
normal.cn: 花园小径是同一种窄走道，只是把墙换成了花。

normal.en: A blind alley ends at a wall, so the phrase means a plan that cannot go on.
normal.cn: blind alley 终止于一堵墙，所以这个短语指无法继续的计划。

normal.en: An alley cat lives in the gaps between buildings, not in a house.
normal.cn: alley cat 住在建筑之间的缝隙里，而不是住在屋里。

abstract.en: Picture two high brick walls almost touching, with a thin strip of sky above them.
abstract.cn: 想象两堵高高的砖墙几乎相碰，上方只留一条细细的天空。

abstract.en: Lay the strip down horizontally and it becomes a lane with a ball rolling along it.
abstract.cn: 把这条缝横过来放平，它就成了一条有球滚过的球道。

abstract.en: Put a wall across the far end and the same strip becomes a blind alley.
abstract.cn: 在远端横上一堵墙，同一条缝就成了死胡同。

examples.en: The delivery van blocked the narrow alley behind the shop.
examples.cn: 送货的面包车堵住了商店后面的窄巷。

examples.en: They spent the afternoon at a bowling alley near the station.
examples.cn: 他们一下午都待在车站附近的保龄球馆。

examples.en: The committee realized the old plan was a blind alley.
examples.cn: 委员会意识到旧方案是一条死胡同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱理」——爱理不理，只肯走那条没人理的小巷

root: 经由古法语 alee（行走、通道）来自拉丁语 ambulare（走动）；本指两墙之间的窄路，后引申指保龄球道、花园小径，并以 blind alley 比喻无出路的办法。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses all keep the shape of a long narrow strip, filled with walls, gutters, plants, or a final barrier.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都保留「长而窄的一条」这个形状，只是填进去的是墙、边沟、植物或一道终点屏障。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two walls stand almost touching, and a thin line of light runs between them toward the far end.
core.cn: 核心意象：两堵墙几乎相贴，一线光在它们之间一直延伸到远端。

branches.en: THE GAP: the first sense is a way for people squeezed between buildings.
branches.cn: 缝隙线：第一个义项是人们在建筑之间挤过去的路。

branches.en: THE LANE: the same strip lies flat and becomes a track for a rolling ball.
branches.cn: 球道线：同一条窄带放平，就成了滚球的轨道。

branches.en: THE GARDEN: walls give way to plants, but the narrow walk remains.
branches.cn: 花园线：墙换成了植物，窄走道仍然保留。

branches.en: THE WALL: when the far end is closed, the passage becomes a metaphor for failure.
branches.cn: 墙线：远端被封住时，通道就成了失败的比喻。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN WAY: an alley is often a route people use to avoid the main street.
branches.cn: 暗线：小巷常是人们避开主街时走的路线。

intro.en: Alley is a French loanword with a small family built by compounding rather than suffixation.
intro.cn: alley 是法语借词，小词族靠复合构词而不是后缀派生。

latinIntro.en: The word goes back to Latin ambulare, but it entered English through French, so the Latin entries are indirect.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词上溯至拉丁语 ambulare，但经法语进入英语，因此拉丁条目是间接的。

items.example: The alley was too narrow for a car.
items.exampleCN: 这条小巷窄得车开不进去。

items.example: It is the distant source of alley.

intro.en: Alligator is a Spanish phrase swallowed whole: el lagarto, the lizard, was applied to the big reptile of the Americas, and English wore it down into one word.
intro.cn: alligator 是一个被整个吞下的西班牙语短语：el lagarto「那只蜥蜴」被用来称呼美洲的大爬行动物，英语把它磨损成一个词。

items.en: Latin lacertus meant lizard, a word still used in zoology for the genus Lacerta.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lacertus 意为蜥蜴，动物学中仍用于 Lacerta 属。

items.en: Spanish lagarto developed from lacertus and named any lizard, large or small.
items.cn: 西班牙语 lagarto 由 lacertus 演变而来，指任何蜥蜴，无论大小。

items.en: Spanish speakers in the Americas called the big reptile el lagarto, the lizard, with the definite article attached.
items.cn: 美洲的西班牙语使用者把这种大爬行动物叫作 el lagarto「那只蜥蜴」，带着定冠词。

items.en: English sailors and settlers heard the phrase as one word and wrote alligator by the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语水手与移民把这个短语听成一个词，到十七世纪已写作 alligator。

items.en: The word now names two living species and, by extension, the scaly leather and the crackle pattern that resembles it.
items.cn: 该词如今指两个现存物种，并引申指鳞状皮革与类似的龟裂纹路。

definition_zh: 分配；拨给；分派（任务）；把（成本）分摊到科目
definition_en: to give out money, time, or resources for a particular purpose, or to assign a duty or cost to someone
core_image: 一张长桌上摆着几只空盘子，厨师按人数把菜一份份分进去
scene: 市政会议开到深夜，争论的焦点是钱该往哪里花。The council allocated half the budget to road repairs.
sceneCN: 这里的 allocate 是「分配、拨给」（第 1 个义项：把钱或资源按用途分出）；句意是市议会把一半预算拨给了道路维修。

senses.title: To give out money or resources
senses.definition: to set apart and give out money, materials, or other resources for a stated purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途划出并发放资金、物资或其他资源
senses.example: The hospital allocated two million pounds to new equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 医院拨出两百万英镑购置新设备。
senses.why: Latin locare meant 'to place', and ad- added 'to'; to allocate is to place something into a particular slot, so money is put where the purpose requires it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 locare 意为「放置」，ad- 表示「到」；allocate 就是「放到某个位置上」，钱被放进为它指定的那一格，所以既可译「分配」也可译「拨给」。

senses.title: To assign a duty or role
senses.definition: to give a particular job, duty, or role to a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 把某项工作、职责或角色交给某个人或某个群体
senses.example: The teacher allocated each group a different part of the project.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把项目的不同部分分派给各个小组。
senses.why: The same 'placing' works for tasks: a duty is put into someone's hands, and the person becomes the slot it occupies.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「放置」也适用于任务：职责被放进某人手里，那个人就成了这项职责所在的位置，因此 allocate 常与 tasks、duties、roles 搭配。

senses.title: To apportion costs in accounting
senses.definition: to divide a cost or revenue among accounts, departments, or periods in bookkeeping
senses.definitionCN: 在记账中把成本或收入分摊到各科目、各部门或各期间
senses.example: The firm allocated the overhead costs across its three branches.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把间接费用分摊到三个分部。
senses.why: In accounting the 'placing' becomes a division: one total is cut into shares and each share is placed on the account that caused it, which is why the verb appears with costs and overhead.
senses.whyCN: 在会计里，「放置」变成了「切分」：一笔总额被切成若干份，每一份放进造成它的那个科目，所以这个义项的宾语常见 costs、overhead 这类词。

intro.en: Allocate is a bookkeeping word at heart: it comes from a Latin verb for placing something in a spot.
intro.cn: allocate 骨子里是个记账词：它来自拉丁语中表示「把东西放到某处」的动词。

items.en: locus meant 'place, spot', and it also gave English local and locate.
items.cn: locus 意为「地方、位置」，英语的 local 与 locate 也由它而来。

items.en: locare meant 'to place, set, arrange', and was used of putting things or persons in position.
items.cn: locare 意为「放置、安置、安排」，用于把物品或人放到位置上。

items.en: The prefixed form allocare is recorded in medieval Latin with the sense 'to place to, assign', especially in accounts.
items.cn: 加前缀的形式 allocare 见于中世纪拉丁语，义为「放置到、分派」，尤用于账目。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century; early examples already concern money and shares.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，早期用例已经与钱款和份额有关。

items.en: Modern usage extends the verb from budgets to tasks, seats, time slots, and computing memory.
items.cn: 现代用法把它从预算扩展到任务、座位、时间段以及计算机内存。

senses.title: The act of sharing out resources
senses.titleCN: 把资源分给各方的行为
senses.definition: the act of dividing something among several users or purposes
senses.definitionCN: 把某物在多个使用者或用途之间分开的行为
senses.example: The committee agreed on an allocation of funds to three research teams.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会同意把经费分配给三个研究团队。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to place something somewhere, so allocation is literally placing each part where it goes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为把某物放到某处，因此 allocation 字面上就是把每一份放到它该去的地方。

senses.title: Resource allocation in economics
senses.definition: the way an economy decides which goods and services get produced and who gets them
senses.definitionCN: 一个经济体决定生产哪些商品与服务、由谁获得的方式
senses.example: Efficient resource allocation is the central question of the course.
senses.exampleCN: 有效的资源配置是这门课的核心问题。
senses.why: Economics studies who gets what, and placing each part is exactly what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 经济学研究谁得到什么，而「把每一份放好」正是这个词所描述的。

senses.title: A budget line or grant
senses.definition: a sum of money set aside for a particular department or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某部门或某用途专门留出的款项
senses.example: The library's allocation rose by five per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆的拨款增加了百分之五。
senses.why: A grant is money placed at a destination, so the word shifts from the act to the sum assigned.
senses.whyCN: 拨款就是把钱放到某个去处，因此词义从动作转到被指派的款额。

senses.title: Assigning duties to people
senses.definition: the assignment of jobs or responsibilities to particular people
senses.definitionCN: 把工作或责任分给具体的人
senses.example: A clear allocation of duties prevented two people editing the same page.
senses.exampleCN: 明确分派职责，避免了两人重复编辑同一页。
senses.why: Tasks are placed on people's desks, which extends the placing image from things to duties.
senses.whyCN: 任务被放到各人的桌上，这把「安放」的意象从物品扩展到职责。

senses.title: A share of limited places
senses.definition: the distribution of limited places such as seats or school positions
senses.definitionCN: 座位、学位等有限名额的分发
senses.example: The allocation of school places followed a new formula.
senses.exampleCN: 学位名额按新公式分配。
senses.why: When places are scarce, sharing them out becomes a visible decision with rules.
senses.whyCN: 当名额稀缺，如何分发就成了一件有规则、看得见的决定。

senses.title: Memory allocation in computing
senses.definition: the process by which a program reserves memory for data
senses.definitionCN: 程序为数据预留内存的过程
senses.example: A memory allocation error crashed the program.
senses.exampleCN: 一次内存分配错误让程序崩溃。
senses.why: Computing reused the word because memory, like money, is a finite store that must be handed out.
senses.whyCN: 计算机沿用这个词，因为内存和钱一样是有限存量，必须逐一派给。

senses.title: Cost allocation in accounting
senses.definition: the assignment of shared costs to the activities or products that caused them
senses.definitionCN: 把共同成本分给造成这些成本的业务或产品
senses.example: Cost allocation put half the warehouse bill on the online orders.
senses.exampleCN: 成本分摊把一半仓储费算到了网络订单上。
senses.why: Accounting places each cost on a product, which is the same gesture applied to figures.
senses.whyCN: 会计把每笔成本放到某个产品上，是同一动作用在数字上。

senses.title: Rationing in times of shortage
senses.definition: the controlled distribution of scarce goods to users, often by quota
senses.definitionCN: 按配额把稀缺物资受控地分给使用者
senses.example: Wartime allocation of sugar limited each household to a small weekly amount.
senses.exampleCN: 战时的食糖配给把每户每周限制在少量。
senses.why: Rationing is sharing out under pressure, so the word takes on the tone of scarcity.
senses.whyCN: 配给就是压力下的分发，因此这个词带上稀缺的意味。

intro.en: Allocation comes from Medieval Latin allocatio, from allocare 'to place, assign', built on ad- 'to' and locus 'place'. English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: allocation 来自中世纪拉丁 allocatio，源自动词 allocare「安放、指派」，由 ad-「向」与 locus「地方」构成，十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: Locus meant 'place, position'. It gives local, locate, locality and dislocate.
items.cn: locus 意为「地方、位置」，衍生 local、locate、locality 与 dislocate。

items.en: Locare meant 'to place, set, station', turning the noun of place into a verb of putting.
items.cn: locare 意为「放置、安顿、驻扎」，把表示地方的名词变成「放」的动词。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus locare gave allocare, 'to place something to someone, assign'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 locare 构成 allocare，意为「把某物放到某人处、指派」。

items.en: Allocatio, 'an assigning', was used in accounts and administration before English borrowed it.
items.cn: allocatio「指派、分派」在英语借入之前已用于账目与行政。

items.en: English adopted the word in the 1500s for the setting aside of money or goods for a purpose.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收这个词，指为某用途留出钱或货。

items.en: Source uncertain: whether English took the noun directly from Latin or through French allocation is not settled, and the earliest date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语是直接从拉丁语借入，还是经法语 allocation 传入，尚无定论；最早年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same place root that are easily confused with allocation; group two holds near terms for sharing out.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「地方」词根、易与 allocation 混淆的词；第二组是表示分发的近义词。

entries.definition: A position or site, from the same place root; it names where something is, not how it is divided.
entries.definitionCN: 位置或地点，同出「地方」词根；指某物在哪，不指如何分。

entries.definition: A share or a small plot assigned to someone, built on lot rather than locus; it is close in meaning but not a relative.
entries.definitionCN: 分给某人的一份或一小块地，由 lot 而非 locus 构成；意思接近但不同源。

entries.definition: To move something out of its proper place, as a joint; it keeps the place image but reverses the fitting.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物移出原位，如关节脱位；保留「地方」意象但把安放反过来。

entries.definition: A formal speech, from loqui 'to speak'; the shared opening is misleading.
entries.definitionCN: 正式讲话，来自 loqui「说话」；相同的开头容易误导。

entries.definition: The general word for spreading things among people or places; it does not imply a decision about shares.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西分给人或地方的通用词；不含「决定份额」之意。

entries.definition: The division of something in fixed proportions, often by rule; it stresses the ratio rather than the placing.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定比例分，常依规则；强调比例而非安放。

entries.definition: The giving of a task or a person to a role; it is the usual word when duties rather than funds are involved.
entries.definitionCN: 把任务或人派到某角色；涉及职责而非资金时更常用。

entries.definition: Controlled distribution of scarce goods by quota; it is the emergency form of allocation.
entries.definitionCN: 按配额受控地分发稀缺物资；是 allocation 的紧急形态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the place root, the fixed phrases and the real family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「地方」词根、固定搭配与真实词族。

normal.en: Ad- 'to' plus locus 'place': to allocate is to put each part in its place.
normal.cn: ad-「向」加 locus「地方」：分配就是把每一份放到它的位置。

normal.en: The family runs allocate, allocation, allocative, allocator, reallocation and misallocation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 allocate、allocation、allocative、allocator、reallocation 与 misallocation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: resource allocation, budget allocation, seat allocation, cost allocation.
normal.cn: 固定说法：资源配置、预算分配、名额分配、成本分摊。

normal.en: The same root appears in local, locate, locality and dislocate.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 local、locate、locality 与 dislocate 中。

normal.en: A budget line is money placed at a destination, so the act and the sum share one word.
normal.cn: 预算中的一项就是把钱放到某个去处，动作与款额因此共用一个词。

abstract.en: Picture a cake cut into shares, each labelled with a name.
abstract.cn: 想象一块饼切成若干份，每份都写着名字。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of identical boxes, each carried to a different desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一排放着相同盒子，每只被搬到不同的桌上。

abstract.en: Picture a limited row of chairs and a list deciding who sits where.
abstract.cn: 想象一排有限的椅子，一份名单决定谁坐哪里。

examples.en: The allocation of water between farms and towns is decided each spring.
examples.cn: 农场与城镇之间的水量分配每年春天决定。

examples.en: A fair allocation of seats gave every department two places.
examples.cn: 公平的名额分配让每个部门得到两个位置。

examples.en: Poor allocation of staff left the busiest ward short-handed.
examples.cn: 人员配置不当让最忙的病区人手不足。
