sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture, placing each part where it belongs: sharing resources, the economic question, a budget line, duties, limited places, computer memory, shared costs and finally wartime rations.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个动作——把每一份放到该去的地方：分配资源、经济问题、预算拨款、职责、有限名额、计算机内存、共同成本，最后是战时配给。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a large cake cut into labelled shares, one for each purpose.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张大饼切成标好用途的若干份。

branches.en: ACT AND SUM: sharing out and the budget line it produces are one gesture seen as process and result.
branches.cn: 动作与款额：分发行为与由此产生的预算项，是同一动作的过程与结果。

branches.en: TWO ECONOMIES: resources and shared costs are both placed on someone's account.
branches.cn: 两种经济：资源与共同成本，都被记到某方的账上。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND PLACES: duties go to desks and places go to applicants, both by a decision.
branches.cn: 人与位置：职责分到桌上，名额分到申请人，都靠一个决定。

branches.en: MACHINE MEMORY: the computer hands out its finite store as money is handed out.
branches.cn: 机器内存：计算机像分钱一样分发有限的存储。

branches.en: SCARCITY: when goods run short, sharing becomes rationing.
branches.cn: 稀缺：物资一紧张，分发就变成配给。

intro.en: Allocation is a Latin verb of placing with a prefix that points it at someone, plus a noun ending.
intro.cn: allocation 是由「放置」的拉丁动词加指向某人的前缀，再加名词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin locus and locare give allocate, location, local and dislocate; ad- directs the placing toward a recipient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 locus 与 locare 衍生 allocate、location、local 与 dislocate；ad- 把「放」指向接受者。

items.structure: Latin prefix (assimilating to al- before l)
items.example: The prefix points the placing at a recipient.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「放置」指向接受者。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of a spot.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「地点」的意思。

items.example: The verb turns place into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「地方」变成动作。

items.example: The board allocated funds to two labs.
items.exampleCN: 董事会把经费分给两个实验室。

items.meaning: the act or result of assigning
items.example: The allocation was announced in June.
Allocative efficiency matters in health care.
items.exampleCN: 配置效率在医疗中很重要。

items.example: Reallocation moved two posts to the new site.
items.exampleCN: 重新分配把两个岗位挪到新址。

items.meaning: a bad or wrong sharing out
items.exampleCN: 配置失当浪费了一半预算。

definition_zh: 津贴；零用钱；限额；免税额；体谅
definition_en: a regular sum of money given for a purpose, a permitted amount, or a sum allowed against tax
core_image: 母亲每周把一个封好的小信封放在孩子书桌上
scene: 开学前，父亲把一张卡交给女儿，说每月会往里打钱。Her parents give her a small allowance each month.
sceneCN: 这里的 allowance 是「零用钱、定期给的钱」（第 1 个义项：按固定周期给的一笔钱）；句意是她父母每月给她一笔不多的零用钱。

pos.zh: 名词：津贴；零用钱；限额；免税额；体谅

derivatives.zh: 派生来源，义为「允许；留出」
由 allow 加 -able 构成，义为「可允许的；可扣除的」
由 dis- 加 allowance 构成，义为「驳回；不准」

senses.title: Money given regularly
senses.definition: a sum of money given regularly, especially by a parent to a child or by an employer for a stated purpose
senses.definitionCN: 按固定周期给的一笔钱，尤指父母给孩子的零用钱，或雇主为特定用途发放的补贴
senses.example: He saves half of his weekly allowance for books.
senses.exampleCN: 他每周的零用钱有一半存起来买书。
senses.why: The noun is allow plus -ance: the sum exists because someone has allowed it, so the money carries the trace of permission granted in advance.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是 allow 加 -ance：这笔钱之所以存在，是因为有人「准许」了它，所以津贴一词本身带着预先获准的痕迹。

senses.title: A permitted amount or limit
senses.definition: an amount of something that rules or conditions permit, such as weight, time, or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 规定或条件所允许的数量，如重量、时间或件数
senses.example: Each passenger has a baggage allowance of twenty kilograms.
senses.exampleCN: 每位乘客的行李限额是二十公斤。
senses.why: Here the permission is measured: instead of money, the word marks the ceiling that has been set, so allowance becomes a limit you must stay under.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「准许」被量化了：不再是一笔钱，而是被划出的上限，于是 allowance 变成不能越过的量，常见于行李、时间、配额等语境。

senses.title: A sum allowed against tax
senses.definition: an amount of income that is not taxed, or a sum that may be deducted before tax is calculated
senses.definitionCN: 不需纳税的收入额度，或在计税前可扣除的金额
senses.example: The personal allowance rises slightly next year.
senses.exampleCN: 个人免税额明年会略微提高。
senses.why: Tax law uses the same idea of a permitted portion: a slice of income is allowed to pass untaxed, and that slice takes the name allowance.
senses.whyCN: 税法沿用同一个「获准的部分」概念：一部分收入被允许不计税地通过，这一部分就叫 allowance，所以它既是「免税额」也是「可扣除额」。

senses.title: Consideration for circumstances
senses.definition: the act of taking special circumstances into account and judging someone less strictly, used in make allowance for
senses.definitionCN: 把特殊情况考虑在内而从宽判断，用于短语 make allowance for
senses.example: We should make allowance for the fact that she was ill.
senses.exampleCN: 我们应该体谅她当时生病这一情况。
senses.why: If an amount can be allowed inside a rule, a person can also be granted a margin; the phrase make allowance for transfers the budgeting image to judgement.
senses.whyCN: 既然规则之内可以「留出」一定量，人也同样可以被「留出」一点余地；make allowance for 把预算里的那点余量转用到对人的评判上。

intro.en: Allowance is simply the noun of allow, and it inherits the word's double Latin ancestry.
intro.cn: allowance 就是 allow 的名词形式，也继承了它双重拉丁词源的血统。

items.en: The verb alouer meant to grant, approve, or assign, and English took it as allow.
items.cn: 动词 alouer 意为准许、认可、分派，英语借入后作 allow。

items.en: The verb's sense of granting a share produced the need for a noun naming the thing granted.
items.cn: 这个动词「准给一份」的意思，催生了一个指称「所准给之物」的名词。

items.en: The noun allowance is recorded from the fourteenth century with the sense of a sum granted or a stated quantity.
items.cn: 名词 allowance 自十四世纪有记录，义为「准给的款项」或「规定的数量」。

items.en: Trade and colonial accounting fixed the money sense, and transport added the measured sense of weight and space allowed.
items.cn: 商业与殖民时期的账务固定了「钱」的义项，运输业则加上按重量与空间计量的「限额」义。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from pocket money to baggage limits and tax thresholds, with make allowance for keeping the older idea of lenient judgement.
items.cn: 现代用法从零用钱延伸到行李限额与免税额，make allowance for 则保留了「从宽判断」的旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on allow; the near-meaning group separates money given from limits set.
note.cn: 形近组由 allow 构成；近义组区分「发放的钱」与「设定的限额」。

definition_zh: 合金：把一种金属与另一种金属或非金属熔合而成的材料；也指掺混、降低成色以及由此引申的混合体
definition_en: a metal made by melting and mixing two or more elements, and the act of mixing metals or of debasing one by adding another
core_image: 熔炉里两种金属液汇合，颜色由亮红转为银白，冷却后的断面均匀一致
scene: 坩埚里铜液与锡液汇合，颜色由亮红转向银白，冷却后的断面看不出两种金属。An alloy of copper and tin is harder than either metal alone.
sceneCN: 这里指合金这种材料（第 1 个义项：两种以上元素熔合而成的金属材料）；句意为铜与锡的合金，比其中任何一种金属都硬。

pos.zh: 合金（材料，可数或不可数）
掺混物；降低成色的成分（常用于比喻）
熔合（金属）；掺杂使降低成色

collocations.phrase: an alloy of copper and tin

alloy + -ing（动名词）→ 合金化，语义偏移为「向金属中有意加入元素的工序」

senses.title: The material
senses.titleCN: 合金：熔合而成的金属材料
senses.definition: a metal produced by melting and mixing two or more elements so that they form one material
senses.definitionCN: 把两种以上元素熔合、混合成一种材料的金属
senses.example: An alloy of copper and tin is harder than either metal alone.
senses.exampleCN: 铜与锡的合金，比其中任何一种金属都硬。
senses.why: Melting lets different metals dissolve into one another; when the melt solidifies, the mixture behaves as a single material, which is why the result gets its own name.
senses.whyCN: 熔炼让不同金属彼此溶解；熔体凝固后，混合物作为一个整体表现，因此产物得到了自己的名称。

senses.title: One recipe
senses.titleCN: 一种配比：特定成分的合金
senses.definition: a particular combination of metals with a stated proportion
senses.definitionCN: 按一定比例配成的特定金属组合
senses.example: The bell is cast from an alloy with about a fifth tin.
senses.exampleCN: 这口钟用一种含锡约五分之一的合金铸成。
senses.why: Once the class exists, each recipe counts as one alloy, because proportions change hardness, colour and sound.
senses.whyCN: 类别义一旦成立，每一种配方就算一种合金，因为比例会改变硬度、颜色与声音。

senses.title: A debasing mixture
senses.titleCN: 掺杂降质：混入物与不纯
senses.definition: something mixed in that lowers the purity or value of a metal, and by extension any unwanted addition
senses.definitionCN: 混入后降低金属纯度或价值的东西，引申为任何不需要的掺杂
senses.example: The gold was accepted without alloy.
senses.exampleCN: 这批黄金被认定毫无掺杂。
senses.why: Adding a cheaper metal to a precious one was a way of cheating weight and value, so the word also carries the sense of a loss of purity.
senses.whyCN: 在贵金属里掺入便宜金属，是偷重量、偷成色的手段，因此这个词也带有「纯净度受损」的含义。

senses.title: To fuse metals
senses.titleCN: 动词：把金属熔合在一起
senses.definition: to melt two or more metals together into one material
senses.definitionCN: 把两种以上金属熔成一种材料
senses.example: They alloy the copper with a little beryllium.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在铜里加入少量铍，熔成合金。
senses.why: The noun's process sense turns into a verb, naming the deliberate act of combining melts rather than the result.
senses.whyCN: 名词的过程义转为动词，命名的是有意把熔体合并的动作，而不是结果。

senses.title: To debase
senses.definition: to lower the quality of a metal by adding a cheaper one
senses.definitionCN: 加入较便宜的金属以降低成色
senses.example: The mint alloyed the silver to stretch the supply.
senses.exampleCN: 铸币厂在银里掺料，以拉长供应。
senses.why: The same verb covers honest metallurgy and dishonest coinage; context decides whether the mixing is a recipe or a fraud.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词既指正当的冶金，也指不正当的铸币；语境决定这种混合是配方还是欺诈。

senses.title: The coinage sense
senses.titleCN: 货币成色：铸币中的合金比例
senses.definition: the proportion of base metal in a coin, as a historical standard of value
senses.definitionCN: 硬币中贱金属所占的比例，历史上作为价值标准
senses.example: The alloy of the coin was fixed by royal decree.
senses.exampleCN: 这种硬币的成色由王室法令规定。
senses.why: Coins were valued by their precious metal content, so the mixing ratio became a matter of law rather than of workshop choice.
senses.whyCN: 硬币的价值取决于贵金属含量，因此配比成了法律问题，而不是作坊选择。

senses.title: The attributive use
senses.titleCN: 定语：合金制的、含合金的
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark an object or material as made of or containing an alloy
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标明某物由合金制成或含有合金
senses.example: Alloy wheels are lighter than steel ones.
senses.exampleCN: 合金轮毂比钢制的轻。
senses.why: A material noun can modify another noun directly, so the same word labels wheels, steel and frames without any ending.
senses.whyCN: 材料名词可以直接修饰另一名词，因此同一个词不加词尾就能标记轮毂、钢与车架。

senses.title: A mixture of anything
senses.titleCN: 比喻：由不同成分构成的混合体
senses.definition: a figurative mixture of different qualities, styles or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义：不同性质、风格或情感构成的混合
senses.example: Her optimism was an alloy of memory and stubbornness.
senses.exampleCN: 她的乐观是记忆与固执的混合体。
senses.why: If a metal can be improved or debased by mixing, then a character or a style can be described as a mixture in the same way, with the same hint of impurity.
senses.whyCN: 既然金属能靠混合而改良或降质，那么性格或风格也可以用同样的方式描述为混合物，并带有同样一丝「不纯」的暗示。

intro.en: Alloy comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to bind to'. The metallurgical sense is the older one; the figurative sense of a mixed or debased thing grows out of it.
intro.cn: alloy 来自一个意为「绑到……上」的拉丁动词。冶金义是较早的一层，混合或降质的比喻义由它生长出来。

items.en: Alligare combined ad- 'to' with ligare 'to bind', and meant to tie or attach something to something else. This derivation is generally accepted and is reflected in the modern spelling.
items.cn: alligare 由 ad-「向」与 ligare「绑」组合而成，意为把某物系到另一物上。这一派生是公认的，并在现代拼写中留下痕迹。

items.en: Old French aloier took the Latin verb and used it for combining metals; the noun aloi named the resulting mixture and passed into English as alloy.
items.cn: 古法语 aloier 承袭这个拉丁动词，并用它指把金属合在一起；名词 aloi 指所得的混合物，进入英语后成为 alloy。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the sixteenth century, first in the language of mints and metal trades, where combining and debasing were practical everyday matters.
items.cn: 这个名词自十六世纪起见于英语，最早出现在铸币与金属行业的话语里，在那里合料与降质是日常实务。

items.en: Because adding a base metal lowers value, the word acquired the sense of an unwanted element mixed into anything, which produced the phrase 'without alloy' for something pure.
items.cn: 因为掺入贱金属会降低价值，这个词获得了「混入任何东西里的不想要成分」之义，并产生「毫无掺杂」这一表示纯净的说法。

items.en: Modern metallurgy uses alloy for any deliberate multi-element metal and for the corresponding verb, and the attributive form labels products such as alloy steel and alloy wheels.
items.cn: 现代冶金用 alloy 指任何有意配成的多元素金属，也指相应的动词；定语形式则标记合金钢、合金轮毂一类产品。

items.en: Dating and sense shift: the exact first English citation is not fixed, and the sense development from 'binding' to 'mixing metals' happened inside French rather than in Latin.
items.cn: 年代与语义转移：确切的英语首见书证没有定论，而从「绑定」到「混合金属」的语义发展发生在法语内部，不在拉丁语中。

note.en: Group one holds words whose shapes invite confusion; group two holds the real neighbouring materials and processes.
note.cn: 第一组是形态上容易混淆的词；第二组是真正相邻的材料与工艺。

entries.definition: To reduce fear or pain, from Old English alecgan 'to lay down'; it sounds like alloy but has a native origin.
entries.definitionCN: 减轻恐惧或疼痛，来自古英语 alecgan「放下」；它读起来像 alloy，但来源是本族的。

entries.definition: A narrow passage between buildings, from Old French alee 'a going'; the ending differs and the sense is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物之间的窄通道，来自古法语 alee「行走」；词尾不同，意义也无关。

entries.definition: A state or person joined to another by agreement, from Latin alligare through French; it shares the root 'to bind' but means a partner, not a material.
entries.definitionCN: 通过协议与他方联合的国家或个人，经法语来自拉丁 alligare；它与 alloy 共享「绑」的词根，但指的是伙伴，不是材料。

entries.definition: Made into an alloy, or mixed with something less pure; a form of the same word, not a separate metal.
entries.definitionCN: 被做成合金的，或掺了较不纯成分的；是同一个词的形式，不是另一种金属。

entries.definition: An alloy in which mercury is the main component, and by extension any blend; it is a special kind of alloy, not a general synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 以汞为主要成分的合金，引申为任何混合物；它是合金的一个特殊种类，不是一般同义词。

entries.definition: A specific copper-tin alloy; alloy is the general class to which bronze belongs.
entries.definitionCN: 特指铜锡合金；alloy 是 bronze 所属的总类。

entries.definition: A material made of distinct components that remain separate, such as fibres in resin; an alloy is chemically mixed, a composite is not.
entries.definitionCN: 由仍保持分离的组分构成的材料，如树脂中的纤维；合金是化学意义上的混合，复合材料不是。

entries.definition: Any mixture, often of things that stay distinguishable; an alloy specifically involves molten metals.
entries.definitionCN: 任何混合物，通常其中成分仍可分辨；合金则专指熔融金属的混合。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb 'to bind', the mint's practical sense, and the real alloy names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁动词「绑」、铸币厂的实务义，以及真实存在的合金名称。

normal.en: The root is 'to bind': ad- plus ligare, so an alloy is metals tied together rather than merely stirred.
normal.cn: 词根是「绑」：ad- 加 ligare，因此合金是被绑在一起的金属，而不只是被搅在一起。

normal.en: The same root gives ally: an ally is bound to you by agreement, an alloy is bound into one material.
normal.cn: 同一词根也给出 ally：盟友靠协议与你绑定，合金则被绑成一种材料。

normal.en: The dishonest sense is old: mints alloyed silver to make more coins from the same weight.
normal.cn: 不诚实的义项很古老：铸币厂在银里掺料，用同样的重量造出更多硬币。

normal.en: The real named alloys are bronze and brass, copper with tin and copper with zinc.
normal.cn: 真实有专名的合金是青铜与黄铜：铜加锡、铜加锌。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the class and the purity: alloy steel, alloy wheel, without alloy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类别与纯度：合金钢、合金轮毂、毫无掺杂。

abstract.en: Picture two melts meeting in one crucible and coming out as a single colour that neither had before.
abstract.cn: 想象两种熔体在同一只坩埚里相遇，出来时是一种两者原本都没有的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a coin whose value is written into its recipe, so the workshop becomes a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币的价值被写进它的配方，于是作坊变成了法庭。

abstract.en: Picture a character described as a mixture: the same word that debases metal now debases a feeling.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人的性格被描述为混合物：同一个曾用来降低金属成色的词，如今在降低一种情感的纯度。

examples.en: The frame is made of a light alloy that resists corrosion.
examples.cn: 这个车架由一种耐腐蚀的轻合金制成。

examples.en: Their joy was real but not without alloy.
examples.cn: 他们的快乐是真的，但并非毫无掺杂。

examples.en: The smith alloyed the copper with tin until the colour matched.
examples.cn: 铁匠在铜里加锡，直到颜色对得上。

dict_mnemonic.text: alloy＝合金；记「ad 向 + ligare 绑，把两种金属绑成一种」。

root: 拉丁 alligare「绑到……上」（ad- + ligare「绑」），经古法语 aloier、aloi 进入英语；由「合料」引申出合金、掺杂与混合体诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one binding: the material, one recipe of it, a debasing addition, the verb of fusing, the verb of debasing, coinage standard, the attributive label, and a mixture of anything.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「绑合」这一动作展开：材料本身、一种配比、降低成色的掺入、熔合的动词、降质的动词、铸币成色、定语标签，以及任何事物的混合体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two molten metals meet in a crucible and solidify as one uniform block.
core.cn: 核心意象：两种熔融金属在坩埚中相遇，凝固成一块均匀的整体。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: mixing by melting produces something that behaves as one metal.
branches.cn: 材料本身：熔融混合产生的材料，表现得像一种金属。

branches.en: THE RECIPE: each set of proportions is a countable alloy with its own properties.
branches.cn: 配比层：每一组成分比例都是可数的一种合金，各有自己的性能。

branches.en: THE LOSS OF PURITY: adding a cheaper metal debases value, and in coinage the ratio becomes law.
branches.cn: 纯净度的损失：掺入便宜金属会降低价值，在铸币中配比还成了法律。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb names the deliberate combining of melts.
branches.cn: 动作层：动词命名有意把熔体合并的行为。

branches.en: THE EXTENSIONS: a material used as a modifier, and any mixture of qualities in a person or style.
branches.cn: 延伸层：作修饰语的材料，以及人或风格中任何性质的混合。

intro.en: Alloy is a borrowed noun and verb; its endings are ordinary English, and it compounds with material words such as steel and wheel.
intro.cn: alloy 是借来的名词兼动词；它接的词尾都是普通英语词尾，也能与 steel、wheel 这类材料或物件词构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin alligare, from ad- and ligare, is the source; the related noun alligatio meant a binding, and the same root reached English again through ally.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是拉丁 alligare，由 ad- 与 ligare 构成；相关名词 alligatio 意为绑缚，同一词根又经 ally 再次进入英语。

an alloy that keeps its strength at extreme heat
items.meaningCN: 在极端高温下仍保持强度的合金

items.exampleCN: 涡轮叶片由高温合金制成。

items.example: Dealloying can make a bronze brittle.
Non-alloy steel is cheaper but softer.
items.exampleCN: 非合金钢更便宜但更软。

definition_zh: 诱惑力；魅力；（动词）诱惑；吸引
definition_en: the power of something to attract or fascinate, especially by promising pleasure or advantage; as a verb, to attract or tempt
core_image: 钓钩上那点闪光，让人忍不住伸手
scene: 那份工作薪水一般，却承诺三年后能独立带队。The allure of running his own team won him over.
sceneCN: 这里 allure 是「诱惑力」（第 1 个义项：让人向往、忍不住被吸引的魅力）；句意为「能自己带队」这一点打动了他。核心画面是钓钩上那点闪光，让人忍不住伸手。

forms.label: 过去式与过去分词（动词）

derivatives.zh: 现在分词作形容词，义为「诱人的；迷人的」
加 -ly 构成，义为「诱人地」
加 -ment 构成，义为「诱惑；诱惑物」

senses.title: The quality that draws you in
senses.definition: the power of something to attract or fascinate, especially by promising pleasure or advantage
senses.definitionCN: 某物吸引或令人着迷的力量，尤指通过承诺快乐或好处
senses.example: The allure of the open road kept him travelling.
senses.exampleCN: 开阔公路的魅力让他一直在路上。
senses.why: Allure comes from a- plus lure, a bait, so the word keeps the fishing picture: something shiny dangles and you move toward it.
senses.whyCN: allure 来自 a- 加 lure「饵」，所以该词保留了钓鱼的画面：有个闪光的东西悬在那里，你就朝它移动。

senses.title: To attract by temptation
senses.definition: to attract or tempt someone, often by offering something desirable, the older verbal use of the word
senses.definitionCN: 吸引或引诱某人，常通过提供令人向往的东西，是该词较早的动词用法
senses.example: The brochure allured them with images of empty beaches.
senses.exampleCN: 这本手册用空无一人的海滩图片吸引他们。
senses.why: Here the bait is actively thrown: the subject does the luring rather than merely possessing the charm.
senses.whyCN: 这里饵是被主动抛出的：主语在「下饵」，而不只是拥有那种魅力。

intro.en: Allure is a- plus lure: the Old French loirre, a falconer bait, gave lure, and English added a- to make both a verb and a noun of attraction.
intro.cn: allure 是 a- 加 lure：古法语 loirre「驯鹰人的诱饵」产生 lure，英语加上 a-，造出表示吸引的动词与名词。

items.en: Old French loirre meant a falconer bait, a piece of meat used to call a hawk back to the fist.
items.cn: 古法语 loirre 指驯鹰人的诱饵，即用来把猎鹰唤回拳头上的一块肉。

items.en: The verb aloirer meant to attract with a bait, built from a-, to, plus loirre.
items.cn: 动词 aloirer 意为「用饵吸引」，由 a-「向」加 loirre 构成。

items.en: Middle English aluren meant to tempt or attract, and the noun alure named the power of attraction.
items.cn: 中古英语 aluren 意为引诱或吸引，名词 alure 指吸引力。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the spelling settled as allure, used of both the charm and the act of charming.
items.cn: 到十六世纪拼写固定为 allure，既指魅力，也指施展魅力的动作。

items.en: Modern use favours the noun, with alluring as the common adjective and the verb now rather literary.
items.cn: 现代用法偏重名词，alluring 是常见形容词，动词如今颇具书面色彩。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the lure family and similar openings; the near-meaning group lists other words for attraction.
note.cn: 形近组保留 lure 词族与相近开头；近义组列出其他表示「吸引」的词。

entries.definition: A bait used to attract.
entries.definitionCN: 用来吸引的诱饵。

entries.definition: Strongly attractive or tempting.
entries.definitionCN: 极具吸引力或诱惑力的。

entries.definition: The act of tempting, or a temptation.
entries.definitionCN: 诱惑的行为，或诱惑物。

entries.definition: To refer to something indirectly.
entries.definitionCN: 间接提及某事。

entries.definition: The power to please and attract.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉悦并吸引人的力量。

entries.definition: The quality of being attractive.
entries.definitionCN: 具有吸引力的性质。

entries.definition: A powerful hold on the attention.
entries.definitionCN: 对注意力的强烈吸引。

entries.definition: Something that draws you toward a want.
entries.definitionCN: 把你拉向某种欲望的东西。

normalIntro.en: Allure is a- plus lure: a bait held out, and the pull you feel toward it.
normalIntro.cn: allure 就是 a- 加 lure：伸出去的饵，以及你感到的那股拉力。

normal.en: Lure is hidden inside allure, so always picture a fishing hook with something shiny.
normal.cn: allure 里面藏着 lure，所以永远想象一个挂着闪光物的钓钩。

normal.en: The noun is usually uncountable: the allure of fame, not an allure.
normal.cn: 名词通常不可数：the allure of fame，不说 an allure。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is the allure of something, with of, not for.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 the allure of something，用 of，不用 for。

normal.en: Alluring is the everyday adjective; the verb allure sounds literary.
normal.cn: alluring 是日常形容词，动词 allure 听起来很书面。

normal.en: Do not confuse allure with allude: one attracts, the other hints.
normal.cn: 别把 allure 与 allude 混淆：一个是吸引，一个是暗示。

abstract.en: Picture a bright feather drifting just above the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一片亮羽毛在水面上方轻轻飘动。

abstract.en: Imagine a shop window that makes you stop without deciding to.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇橱窗，让你不由自主地停下脚步。

abstract.en: Think of a promise hanging at the end of a thin line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个承诺悬在一根细线的末端。

examples.en: The allure of quick money blinded him to the risk.
examples.cn: 快钱的诱惑让他看不见风险。

examples.en: The old town has lost none of its allure.
examples.cn: 这座老城丝毫未减它的魅力。

examples.en: They were allured by the promise of free land.
examples.cn: 他们被免费土地的承诺所吸引。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿路尔」——阿（a）路（l）尔（lure）：路上挂着饵，把你一路引过去，就是诱惑力、魅力。

root: 古法语 loirre「驯鹰人的诱饵」加前缀 a- 构成 aloirer「用饵吸引」，经中古英语 aluren 演变为 allure，名词指吸引力，动词指引诱，字面即「把饵伸向你」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one bait seen from two sides: the noun names the pull you feel, and the verb names the act of holding out something that pulls.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个饵的两面：名词指你感到的那股拉力，动词指把会拉人的东西伸出去这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shiny bait that makes you reach out
core.cn: 核心意象：一点闪光的饵让你忍不住伸手

branches.en: Fame glittering at a distance.
branches.cn: 名声在远处闪光。

branches.en: A city that promises a new life.
branches.cn: 一座承诺新生活的城市。

branches.en: A brochure holding out empty beaches.
branches.cn: 一本手册伸出空无一人的海滩。

branches.en: A recruiter dangling a promotion.
branches.cn: 招聘者悬着一个升职机会。

branches.en: Both work by holding out a bait.
branches.cn: 两者都靠伸出诱饵起作用。

intro.en: Allure is a- plus lure, and from that bait come alluring, allurement and the plain verb lure itself.
intro.cn: allure 是 a- 加 lure，从这个「饵」派生出 alluring、allurement 以及动词 lure 本身。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin layer: it came from Old French loirre, a falconer bait of Germanic origin, with the prefix a- added in French.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁语层次：它来自古法语 loirre「驯鹰人的诱饵」，源于日耳曼语，前缀 a- 是在法语中加上的。

latinEntries.exampleCN: aloirer 是 allure 的来源。

definition_zh: 冲积的；冲积土的
definition_en: relating to sediment deposited by flowing water, especially at the mouth of a river
core_image: 河流入海口扇形展开的冲积平原，远处是茂密的芦苇和稻田
scene: 纪录片里解说员说：The Ganges delta is one of the largest alluvial plains on earth.
sceneCN: 这里指「由河水带来的泥沙堆积而成的平原」（第1个义项：冲积沉积物的）；句意为恒河三角洲是地球上最大的冲积平原之一。

pos.zh: 冲积的；与冲积物有关的

冲积物（alluvium 的复数）
洪水；冲积作用（较旧）

senses.title: Pertaining to sediment laid down by rivers
senses.titleCN: 与河流淤积的沉积物有关的
senses.definition: describes material carried and deposited by flowing water, not by wind or ice
senses.definitionCN: 描述被水流搬运并沉积的物质，不包括风或冰
senses.example: Alluvial soils are among the most fertile for farming.
senses.exampleCN: 冲积土壤是最肥沃的农田土壤。
senses.why: The root lav- means 'to wash', and a river washes sediment downstream before dropping it.
senses.whyCN: 词根 lav- 意为「洗」，河流把泥沙冲下去再放下。

senses.title: Alluvial plains and deltas
senses.definition: flat areas built up over thousands of years by rivers flooding their banks and dropping sediment
senses.definitionCN: 数千年来由河流漫溢、泥沙沉积而成的平坦区域
senses.example: The Nile delta is a huge alluvial plain supporting 60 million people.
senses.exampleCN: 尼罗河三角洲是养活六千万人的巨大冲积平原。
senses.why: Alluvial plains are the river's way of saving its sediment from washing all the way to the sea.
senses.whyCN: 冲积平原是河流不让泥沙一路冲进海里的办法。

senses.title: Alluvial fans at mountain mouths
senses.definition: fan-shaped deposits where a mountain stream suddenly slows and spreads on flatter ground
senses.definitionCN: 山间溪流突然在平坦地面上减速散开时形成的扇形沉积
senses.example: The valley is dotted with alluvial fans from the surrounding mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷里点缀着周围群山形成的冲积扇。
senses.why: The fan shape comes from the stream opening up like a hand as it leaves the canyon.
senses.whyCN: 扇形来自溪流离开峡谷后像手一样展开。

senses.title: Alluvial minerals and placer deposits
senses.definition: valuable minerals washed free from bedrock and concentrated in river beds, such as gold and diamonds
senses.definitionCN: 从基岩里被冲出来、在河床里富集的贵矿物，如金和钻石
senses.example: The California gold rush was mostly mining alluvial deposits, not hard rock.
senses.exampleCN: 加州淘金潮主要挖的是冲积砂矿，不是硬岩。
senses.why: Heavy minerals sink while lighter sand continues downstream; prospectors sift for the heavy ones.
senses.whyCN: 重矿物沉底，轻沙继续往下漂；找矿人筛的就是重的那些。

senses.title: Alluvial aquifers underground
senses.definition: porous sand and gravel layers laid down by ancient rivers that hold groundwater
senses.definitionCN: 古河流沉积的多孔沙砾层，里面储存着地下水
senses.example: Most drinking water in the Midwest comes from alluvial aquifers.
senses.exampleCN: 美国中西部大部分饮用水来自冲积含水层。
senses.why: Alluvial gravel is porous, making it an ideal natural water container.
senses.whyCN: 冲积砾石多孔，是天然理想的储水容器。

senses.title: Figurative: layers of accumulated ideas
senses.definition: used for layers of culture or thought built up gradually over generations
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述几代人逐渐堆积起来的文化或思想层
senses.example: The city's dialect is an alluvial deposit of migrations from a dozen regions.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的方言是来自十几个地区移民的冲积层。
senses.why: Each group arrives like a river bringing sediment, and the speech of the whole community changes.
senses.whyCN: 每群人到达就像一条河带来泥沙，整个社区的语言就改变了。

senses.title: Alluvial vs colluvial distinction
senses.definition: geologists distinguish alluvial (water-carried) from colluvial (gravity-carried) deposits
senses.definitionCN: 地质学家区分水搬运的冲积和重力搬运的塌积
senses.example: The sample turned out to be colluvial, not alluvial as the farmer had guessed.
senses.exampleCN: 样本原来是塌积的，不是农民猜的冲积。
senses.why: Different transport mechanisms leave different particle shapes and sorting.
senses.whyCN: 不同搬运方式留下不同颗粒形状和分选程度。

senses.title: Agricultural use and management
senses.definition: farmers prize alluvial soils but must manage them to prevent nutrient loss and subsidence
senses.definitionCN: 农民珍惜冲积土壤，但要防止养分流失和土地下沉
senses.example: Intensive irrigation is gradually depleting the alluvial aquifer.
senses.exampleCN: 过度灌溉正在慢慢耗尽冲积含水层。
senses.why: Decades of agriculture draw down the ancient alluvial groundwater faster than rain can refill it.
senses.whyCN: 几十年农业抽取古冲积地下水的速度快过雨水补充。

intro.en: alluvial comes from Latin alluere, itself from ad- (to) + lavare (to wash); the -al suffix makes it an adjective describing what has been washed.
intro.cn: alluvial 来自拉丁语 alluere，拆成 ad-（向）+ lavare（洗）；-al 后缀让它变成形容词，描述「被洗下来的」东西。

items.en: lavare = to wash. alluere = to wash against, to wash down. Latin alluvium meant 'matter deposited by water' since at least the 1st century BCE.
items.cn: lavare = 洗。alluere = 冲着洗、往下冲。至少公元前 1 世纪，拉丁语 alluvium 就指「水冲下来的堆积物」。

items.en: English alluvium appeared as a noun in the 16th century in geological writing.
items.cn: 英语 alluvium 在 16 世纪的地质文献里作为名词出现。

items.en: alluvial was formed by adding the Latin -alis adjective suffix, first recorded in the late 17th century.
items.cn: alluvial 通过加拉丁 -alis 形容词后缀构成，最早记载于 17 世纪末。

items.en: As geology matured in the 18th century, alluvial became a key classification for sedimentary deposits.
items.cn: 18 世纪地质学成熟时，alluvial 变成了沉积岩分类的关键词。

items.en: During the California Gold Rush, prospectors learned to distinguish alluvial gold from hard-rock veins.
items.cn: 加州淘金潮时，探矿人学会了区分冲积金和硬岩矿脉。

items.en: alluvial remains a technical term in geography, geology, and water management.
items.cn: alluvial 至今仍是地理、地质和水管理领域的技术术语。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the lav- wash family; the near-meaning group lists other terms for sediment deposited by water, ice or gravity.
note.cn: 形近组留在 lav-「洗」词根家族内；近义组列出其他表示由水、冰或重力堆积的沉积物的术语。

entries.definition: The noun: the sediment itself, especially a single deposit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词：沉积物本身，尤指单一堆积。

entries.definition: Plural of alluvium, multiple deposits.
entries.definitionCN: alluvium 的复数，多个沉积物。

entries.definition: A place for washing; shares lav- but not the allu- direction.
entries.definitionCN: 洗的地方；共享 lav- 词根但方向不同。

entries.definition: Actually from labi 'to fall', not lavare; similarity is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 实际来自 labi「落」，不是 lavare；相似是巧合。

entries.definition: Sediment carried by gravity, not water: a hillside slide deposit.
entries.definitionCN: 由重力搬运的沉积物，不是水：山坡滑下的堆积。

entries.definition: General term for things related to rivers; alluvial is a specific fluvial process.
entries.definitionCN: 与河流有关的泛指；alluvial 是 fluvial 里的一个具体过程。

entries.definition: Sediment deposited where river meets tide, mixing alluvial and marine processes.
entries.definitionCN: 河海交汇处的沉积物，混合冲积和海洋过程。

entries.definition: Sediment deposited by ice, not water or wind.
entries.definitionCN: 冰沉积的沉积物，不是水或风。

normalIntro.en: alluvial = washed down by a river.
normalIntro.cn: alluvial = 被河「洗」下来的。

normal.en: ad- (to) + lavare (wash) → wash down → alluvial.
normal.cn: ad-（向）+ lavare（洗）→ 冲下去 → alluvial。

normal.en: Alluvial gold sits in river beds where water washed the nuggets free.
normal.cn: 冲积金在河床里，那里的河把金块冲出来了。

normal.en: The Mississippi and Ganges built their deltas from alluvial soil.
normal.cn: 密西西比河和恒河用 alluvial 土壤堆出了三角洲。

normal.en: Farmers love alluvial soil because it comes fresh every flood.
normal.cn: 农民爱 alluvial 土壤，因为每次洪水都带来新的。

normal.en: A geologist's notebook separates alluvial from colluvial samples.
normal.cn: 地质学家笔记本里把 alluvial 和 colluvial 分开写。

abstract.en: A river fanning out at a delta, slowing, dropping its load, building new land.
abstract.cn: 一条河在三角洲散开、减速、卸货、造新陆地。

abstract.en: Layers of fine silt stacked like pages in a very old book.
abstract.cn: 像旧书页一样一页页叠起来的细淤泥。

abstract.en: Heavy gold flakes panning down through lighter sand at the bottom of a pan.
abstract.cn: 淘金盘里在较轻的沙子中间沉底的金片。

examples.en: Flood events renew alluvial fertility every few years in the Mekong delta.
examples.cn: 湄公河三角洲每隔几年的洪水恢复冲积土壤的肥力。

examples.en: The city sits on alluvial deposits up to 200 meters deep, above an ancient river bed.
examples.cn: 这座城市建在厚达 200 米的冲积沉积物上，底下是古河床。

examples.en: Prospectors still sift the river's gravel for alluvial gold on weekends.
examples.cn: 周末还有探矿人在河砾里筛冲积金。

sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项讲「被冲下来的东西」最终留在了哪里：平原、三角洲、扇、矿床、含水层、文化、地质区分、农场。

core.cn: 核心意象：河流离开峡谷进入平原时堆出一个扇形泥沙堆。

branches.en: GEOLOGICAL FORMATIONS AND THEIR USE: plains, deltas and fans are read as landforms and as farmland.
branches.cn: 地质构造与利用：平原、三角洲与冲积扇既是地貌，也是被耕作的田地。

intro.cn: alluvial 是名词 alluvium 加拉丁形容词后缀 -al 构成；alluvium 又来自 alluere「冲着洗」。

latinIntro.en: lavare is a common Latin root giving English launder, lavender (from washing scent), lavatory, deluge.
latinIntro.cn: lavare 是常见拉丁词根，给出 launder（洗衣）、lavatory、deluge（洪水）等。

definition_zh: 杏仁；扁桃仁；扁桃树；杏仁色（浅褐米色）
definition_en: the edible seed of the almond tree, oval and pointed at both ends, eaten as a nut or ground into flour; also a pale warm brown colour
core_image: 一颗藏在硬壳里、两头尖尖的浅褐色种子
scene: 她把坚果磨成粉，做成了圣诞蛋糕。Almond flour gives the cake its dense texture.
sceneCN: 这里 almond 是「杏仁」（第 1 个义项：扁桃树的种子，常作坚果食用）；句意为杏仁粉让蛋糕质地紧实。核心画面是一颗藏在硬壳里、两头尖尖的浅褐色种子。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ine 构成，义为「以杏仁烹制的」
同希腊词根，义为「杏仁状体；大脑杏仁核」
加 -in 构成，义为「杏仁苷」

senses.title: The nut of the almond tree
senses.definition: the edible seed of the almond tree, oval and pointed at both ends, eaten as a nut or ground into flour
senses.definitionCN: 扁桃树的可食种子，椭圆形、两端尖，作坚果食用或磨成粉
senses.example: She scattered toasted almonds over the salad.
senses.exampleCN: 她把烤过的杏仁撒在沙拉上。
senses.why: The word came from Greek amygdale, almond, through Latin and French, and the l was reinserted by scholars who knew the Latin spelling.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自希腊语 amygdale「杏仁」，经拉丁语与法语传入，其中的 l 是懂拉丁拼写的学者重新加回去的。

senses.title: A pale warm brown colour
senses.definition: a pale, slightly warm brown colour like the skin of the nut, used in design and cosmetics
senses.definitionCN: 像杏仁外皮那样浅而略暖的褐色，用于设计与化妆品
senses.example: The walls were painted a soft almond.
senses.exampleCN: 墙面漆成了柔和的杏仁色。
senses.why: Here the nut lends its skin colour to the word, the same transfer that gives us chocolate, olive and salmon.
senses.whyCN: 这里坚果把它外皮的颜色借给了这个词，与 chocolate、olive、salmon 的转移方式相同。

intro.en: Almond travelled from Greek amygdale through Latin amygdala and Old French almande; the l in the modern spelling is a scholarly restoration.
intro.cn: almond 从希腊语 amygdale 经拉丁语 amygdala 与古法语 almande 一路走来；现代拼写中的 l 是学者恢复的。

items.en: Greek amygdale meant almond, and it also named anything shaped like one, including a part of the brain.
items.cn: 希腊语 amygdale 意为杏仁，也指任何杏仁形状的东西，包括大脑的一个部分。

items.en: Latin amygdala kept both the nut and the shape sense, and gave English the anatomical term amygdala.
items.cn: 拉丁语 amygdala 保留坚果与形状两义，并为英语提供解剖学术语 amygdala。

items.en: Old French almande lost the g and the y, and the word entered Middle English as almande or almaunde.
items.cn: 古法语 almande 丢掉了 g 与 y，该词以 almande 或 almaunde 的形式进入中古英语。

items.en: Scribes who knew Latin put the l back, and by the fifteenth century almond was the usual spelling.
items.cn: 懂拉丁语的书吏把 l 加了回去，到十五世纪 almond 成为常见拼写。

items.en: Modern almond names the nut, the tree, its milk and flour, and a pale brown colour used in design.
items.cn: 现代 almond 指坚果、树、它的奶与粉，以及设计中用到的一种浅褐色。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps words of similar shape; the near-meaning group lists other nuts and a neighbouring colour.
note.cn: 形近组保留形状相近的词；近义组列出其他坚果与相邻的颜色。

entries.definition: Nearly, but not quite.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎，但还差一点。

entries.definition: Money given to the poor.
entries.definitionCN: 施舍给穷人的钱。

entries.definition: To change something for the better.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物改得更好。

entries.definition: Cooked or garnished with almonds.
entries.definitionCN: 用杏仁烹制或点缀的。

entries.definition: A wrinkled nut in a hard round shell.
entries.definitionCN: 硬圆壳里带皱纹的坚果。

entries.definition: A small round brown nut.
entries.definitionCN: 小而圆的褐色坚果。

entries.definition: A kidney-shaped nut.
entries.definitionCN: 肾形的坚果。

entries.definition: A pale sandy brown colour.
entries.definitionCN: 浅沙褐色。

normalIntro.en: Almond comes from Greek amygdale, and the brain amygdala is named after the same nut shape.
normalIntro.cn: almond 来自希腊语 amygdale，大脑的 amygdala（杏仁核）正是按同一种坚果形状命名的。

normal.en: Almond and amygdala share one Greek root, so the brain region is literally almond-shaped.
normal.cn: almond 与 amygdala 共享一个希腊词根，所以那个脑区字面就是「杏仁形的」。

normal.en: The l is written but not pronounced: say AH-mund, not AL-mond.
normal.cn: l 写出来但不发音：读作 AH-mund，不是 AL-mond。

normal.en: Almond flour is ground nuts; almond milk is soaked and blended nuts.
normal.cn: almond flour 是磨碎的坚果，almond milk 是浸泡后打碎的坚果。

normal.en: It is countable as a nut, so say six almonds, but uncountable as a colour.
normal.cn: 指坚果时可数，所以说 six almonds；指颜色时不可数。

normal.en: Botanically the almond is a seed, not a true nut, but the kitchen calls it a nut.
normal.cn: 植物学上杏仁是种子，不是真正的坚果，但厨房里叫它坚果。

abstract.en: Picture a pointed brown seed inside a woody shell.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗两头尖的褐色种子藏在木质硬壳里。

abstract.en: Imagine an orchard of small trees with pale pink blossom.
abstract.cn: 想象一片小树林，开着淡粉色的花。

abstract.en: Think of a colour card the shade of the nut skin.
abstract.cn: 想象一张色卡，正是坚果外皮的那个色度。

examples.en: The recipe calls for ground almonds and no wheat flour.
examples.cn: 这个配方要用杏仁粉，不用小麦面粉。

examples.en: Almond trees blossom early in the valley.
examples.cn: 山谷里的扁桃树开花很早。

examples.en: She chose almond for the bedroom walls.
examples.cn: 她为卧室墙面选了杏仁色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿蒙德」——阿（al）蒙（mon）德（d）：硬壳里蒙着一颗尖头种子，就是杏仁。

root: 希腊语 amygdale「杏仁」经拉丁语 amygdala 与古法语 almande 进入中古英语，懂拉丁语的书吏把 l 加回拼写，形成 almond；同一词根还产生解剖学词 amygdala「杏仁核」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses come from one seed: the first names the nut you eat, and the second borrows the pale brown of its skin as a colour name.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都来自同一颗种子：第一个指你吃的坚果，第二个借它外皮的浅褐色作为颜色名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pointed brown seed in a hard shell
core.cn: 核心意象：硬壳里一颗两头尖的褐色种子

branches.en: A handful of toasted nuts.
branches.cn: 一把烤过的坚果。

branches.en: Flour ground from blanched kernels.
branches.cn: 用去皮仁磨成的粉。

branches.en: A pale warm wall colour.
branches.cn: 浅而暖的墙面色。

branches.en: A lipstick shade named after the skin.
branches.cn: 以外皮命名的唇膏色号。

branches.en: Both start from the same seed.
branches.cn: 两者都从同一颗种子出发。

intro.en: Almond has no productive English affixes, but its Greek root amygdal- still builds scientific words, and -ine forms the cooking adjective.
intro.cn: almond 没有能产的英语词缀，但它的希腊词根 amygdal- 仍在造科学词，-ine 则构成烹饪形容词。

latinIntro.en: Greek amygdale passed into Latin amygdala and then into Old French almande, where the g and y were lost.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 amygdale 进入拉丁语成为 amygdala，再进入古法语成为 almande，途中丢掉了 g 与 y。

definition_zh: 字母表；字母系统
definition_en: the set of letters used for writing a language, arranged in a fixed order
core_image: 墙上挂着一张从 A 排到 Z 的字母表
scene: 幼儿园的墙上贴着一张大大的字母表，孩子们每天跟着念。The children sang the alphabet together before class.
sceneCN: 这里 alphabet 是「字母表」（第 1 个义项：一种语言全部字母的固定排列）；句意是上课前孩子们一起唱字母歌。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：按字母顺序的
副词：按字母顺序地
动词：按字母顺序排列
名词：按字母编排

senses.title: The letters of a language
senses.titleCN: 字母表（全部字母的集合）
senses.definition: the complete set of letters that a written language uses
senses.definitionCN: 一种书面语言所使用的全部字母的总和
senses.example: The English alphabet has twenty-six letters.
senses.exampleCN: 英语字母表有二十六个字母。
senses.why: The word began as the names of the first two Greek letters, alpha and beta, and those two names came to stand for the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是希腊头两个字母 alpha 与 beta 的名字，后来这两个名字就代表整套字母。

senses.title: A fixed ordering
senses.definition: the conventional sequence of those letters, used for listing and looking things up
senses.definitionCN: 这些字母约定俗成的先后次序，用于排列条目与查找
senses.example: Names on the list are arranged by alphabet, not by age.
senses.exampleCN: 名单上的名字按字母顺序排列，而不是按年龄。
senses.why: Because the alphabet is learned as an ordered recitation, the word also names the order itself, which is how dictionaries and indexes work.
senses.whyCN: 因为字母表是作为有次序的背诵内容学会的，所以这个词也指这套次序本身，字典与索引正是靠它编排。

intro.en: Alphabet is a rare word whose history is visible in its first two sounds.
intro.cn: alphabet 是个少见的词，它的来历就写在开头两个音里。

items.en: Alpha was the name of the first letter, borrowed from a Phoenician letter meaning 'ox'.
items.cn: alpha 是第一个字母的名称，借自腓尼基字母，原意为「牛」。

items.en: Beta named the second letter and is the source of the English word beta.
items.cn: beta 是第二个字母的名称，也是英语 beta 的来源。

items.en: The Greeks joined the two names into alphabetos, a name for the whole set of letters.
items.cn: 希腊人把两个名字连成 alphabetos，用来指整套字母。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as alphabetum, and the learned languages of Europe passed it on.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 alphabetum，欧洲的学术语言再把它传下去。

items.en: English alphabet appears in the sixteenth century and later yields alphabetical and alphabetize.
items.cn: 英语 alphabet 在十六世纪出现，后来派生出 alphabetical 与 alphabetize。

definition_zh: 改变；更改；（把衣服）改小或改大
definition_en: to change something, or to become different, often in a partial way
core_image: 裁缝把一条过长的裤脚卷起、重新缝好
scene: 裁缝量了量裤脚，说可以改短两厘米，明天就能取。The tailor altered the trousers to fit me.
sceneCN: 这里 alter 是「改（衣服）」（第 3 个义项：通过缝改使衣物合身）；句意是裁缝把裤子改得合我的身。

derivatives.zh: 名词：改动；修改
形容词：改变了的
形容词：可改变的
形容词：不可改变的
名词：替代方案，与 alter 同源

senses.title: To change something partly
senses.definition: to make something different, usually by changing part of it rather than replacing it entirely
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变得不同，通常是改动其中一部分，而不是整体替换
senses.example: The new evidence altered the course of the investigation.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据改变了调查的方向。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin alter, 'the other of two', so to alter is to make a thing other than it was, a shift rather than a total replacement.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」，所以 alter 是让事物变成与原来不同的另一个样子，是转变而不是整体替换。

senses.title: To become different
senses.definition: to change by itself over time, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 自身随时间发生变化，不带宾语
senses.example: Her expression altered when she heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息，她的表情变了。
senses.why: Because the change can happen without an agent, the verb also works intransitively, describing a state that shifts rather than someone acting on it.
senses.whyCN: 因为变化可以在没有施动者的情况下发生，这个动词也可作不及物用法，描述状态自身发生转变。

senses.title: To adjust clothing
senses.definition: to take in or let out a garment so that it fits better
senses.definitionCN: 把衣服收小或放宽，使其更合身
senses.example: The tailor altered the trousers to fit me.
senses.exampleCN: 裁缝把裤子改得合我的身。
senses.why: Tailoring is change on a small scale: the garment stays the same object but its measurements are made other, which is exactly the Latin sense in daily use.
senses.whyCN: 裁缝做的就是小尺度改动：衣服还是那件衣服，只是尺寸被改成另一个样子，这正是 alter 的拉丁本义在日常中的体现。

intro.en: Alter goes back to a Latin word for 'the other of two', which explains why it means change rather than replace.
intro.cn: alter 可追溯到拉丁语「两者中的另一个」，这解释了它为何意为改变而非替换。

items.en: alter meant 'the other one of two', as in alter ego, a second self.
items.cn: alter 意为「两者中的另一个」，如 alter ego 指第二个自我。

items.en: The verb alterare meant 'to make other, to change'.
items.cn: 动词 alterare 意为「使成为另一个、改变」。

items.en: French passed the verb on as alterer, used for changing plans, words, or goods.
items.cn: 法语以 alterer 传下这个动词，用于改变计划、言辞或货物。

items.en: English alter appears in the fourteenth century with the sense 'to make different'.
items.cn: 英语 alter 在十四世纪出现，意为「使不同」。

items.en: The clothing sense grew from everyday tailoring, while alteration names any change made.
items.cn: 衣物义从日常裁缝发展而来，而 alteration 泛指任何改动。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the homophone altar; the near-meaning group grades kinds of change.
note.cn: 形近组区分同音词 altar；近义组按改动方式分级。

normal.en: Altar with an a at the end is the church table.

normal.en: A tailor alters clothes, a planner alters plans.

abstract.cn: 想象裤脚被缝高了一点。

abstract.en: See a road bending away from its old line.
abstract.cn: 想象道路偏离原来的走向。

abstract.en: Watch a face change at a piece of news.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸听到消息后变了神情。

examples.en: Nothing can alter the fact that the deadline has passed.
examples.cn: 截止日期已过，这个事实无法改变。

examples.en: The tailor altered the dress for the wedding.
examples.cn: 裁缝为婚礼改了这条裙子。

examples.en: His mood altered as soon as the rain stopped.
examples.cn: 雨一停，他的心情就变了。

definition_zh: 交替；轮流；使交替发生（形容词：交替的；间隔的；备选的）
definition_en: to take place by turns, or (of things) occurring by turns; every other one; a substitute
core_image: 左右脚一步一步轮流落地
scene: 红灯绿灯按节奏轮流亮起。Red and green lights alternate at the crossing.
sceneCN: 这里的 alternate 是「交替」（第 1 个义项：按次序轮流出现）；句意是路口的红绿灯轮流亮起。

derivatives.zh: 由 alternate 加 -ion 构成，义为「交替；轮换」
现在分词形容词，义为「交替的」
同根词，义为「选择；可选的」，侧重「替代选项」
由 alternate 加 -ly 构成，义为「交替地」

senses.title: To occur by turns
senses.definition: to happen one after the other in a repeating two-part pattern
senses.definitionCN: 以两部分重复的次序先后发生
senses.example: Days of rain alternated with bright mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 雨天与晴朗的早晨交替出现。
senses.why: The Latin alternus means "one after the other": two things taking turns.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alternus 意为「一个接一个」：两物轮换。

senses.title: To cause to take turns
senses.definition: to arrange for two things or people to follow each other in turn
senses.definitionCN: 安排两事物或两人依次轮换
senses.example: The coach alternated the two goalkeepers.
senses.exampleCN: 教练让两名门将轮换上场。
senses.why: The transitive use arranges the same taking of turns.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法就是安排这种轮换。

senses.title: Occurring every other one
senses.definition: happening on every second occasion, skipping one
senses.definitionCN: 每两次发生一次，跳过一次
senses.example: The market is open on alternate Saturdays.
senses.exampleCN: 市场每隔一个周六开市。
senses.why: With only two slots, taking turns means every other one.
senses.whyCN: 只有两个位置时，轮换就意味着每隔一个。

senses.title: Placed one after the other
senses.definition: of things in a row, following one another in a repeating pattern
senses.definitionCN: 一列事物按重复模式依次排列
senses.example: Alternate stripes of black and white.
senses.exampleCN: 黑白相间的条纹。
senses.why: The turn-taking pattern frozen into an arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 轮换模式凝固成排列方式。

senses.title: Serving as a substitute
senses.definition: available or used in place of the usual one
senses.definitionCN: 可替代通常事物或供其代替使用的
senses.example: They found an alternate route around the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 他们找到一条绕过洪水的替代路线。
senses.why: The one who takes the other turn is the substitute.
senses.whyCN: 轮到另一次的那个就是替代者。

senses.title: A person who substitutes
senses.definition: a person ready to act in place of another, as an alternate delegate
senses.definitionCN: 准备顶替他人的人，如候补代表
senses.example: She attended the board as an alternate.
senses.exampleCN: 她以候补身份参加了董事会。
senses.why: The substitute sense becomes a noun for the person.
senses.whyCN: 替代义转为指人的名词。

senses.title: Reciprocal or mutual action
senses.definition: of actions exchanged back and forth between two parties
senses.definitionCN: 两方之间往复交换的动作
senses.example: The negotiators alternate offers and rebuttals.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判者轮流出价与反驳。
senses.why: Taking turns implies exchange; the turn returns.
senses.whyCN: 轮换暗含交换：这一轮还会回来。

senses.title: Alternating current sense
senses.definition: of electric current, reversing direction periodically, as in alternating current
senses.definitionCN: 指电流周期性反向，如交流电
senses.example: Household power is alternating current.
senses.exampleCN: 家用电是交流电。
senses.why: The turn-taking pattern applied to the direction of flow.
senses.whyCN: 轮换模式应用于电流方向。

entries.definition: a dispute; "othering" each other in argument.

entries.definition: to take turns in a cycle, often of more than two.

entries.definition: to give back in return; the exchange side of alternation.

entries.definition: to switch places or exchange repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 反复互换。

abstract.en: A chess clock slapped in turn by two players.
abstract.cn: 两位棋手轮流拍按棋钟。

examples.en: The two hosts alternate each week.
examples.cn: 两位主持人每周轮换。

examples.en: Take an alternate road to avoid the jam.
examples.cn: 换条替代路线避开拥堵。

examples.en: Hope and fear alternated in her letters.
examples.cn: 希望与恐惧在她的信中交替出现。
